chapters.title: Chapter 51: Leveling Up (2)
paragraphs: At once he tried to absorb them all, but on the first try, it didn’t work as last time he had held the core with his hand to absorb, but this time there was no physical touch. The targets were hundreds of cores.
’I need a connection with the cores.’

He spread his mana around the cores and once again tried to absorb the core. This time it worked. He could feel new pure mana entering his body. It took about a minute to absorb all the cores, as no traces of cores were left inside the room.
Leon felt he could have done it faster if he had tried, as most of the time was taken at the start of the process. Once he got used to it, it was quick.
His body felt like it was getting stronger to new degrees, and also the same feeling of his increase in mana and intelligence.
He felt like he could break stone with punches now.
He had expected it but not to this degree, as this time only two messages appeared in front of him in the form of transparent shimmering golden screens.
[You have reached Level 5]
[You have reached Level 6]
If Leon had known the actual rank of those monsters he had killed, he would have been fuming right now.

He was done with all the mana stones he had collected inside the dungeon. It was time for him to use the skill stones, which he was quite excited to use, especially the epic-ranked skill he had gotten from the throne room monster.

He took out both skill stones at the same time. Both of them were around the same size and looked like oval-shaped stones. One was green in color while having strange yellow runes on it, and the other one was orange with strange drawings on it which looked much more complex than the previous one.

He could tell which skill rune was which but still decided to use that function of the system he had used before without knowing to see the information of Seraphine and her master. With just a thought, two shimmering golden notifications popped up in front of his eyes.
’It works. I wasn’t just a fluke.’
[Skill Rune – Lightning Bolt (Common Rank)]
[Skill Rune - King’s Touch (Epic Rank)]

He tried to absorb the common rank lightning bolt skill just like he had absorbed the mana core earlier. A yellow-colored light burst out of the stone, shocking him a little. He tried to dodge, but it entered the space between his temples.
New information started to flood his mind about the skill. After a second it stopped, as now he knew everything about the skill.
He didn’t stop and now moved on to the next skill rune. Just like before, a light entered his temple. He didn’t dodge like the last time.

The information about the skill named King’s Touch entered his mind. After getting the information, now he understood how, before launching his spear of judgment, when he had tried to cut off its head, his blade had stopped at the last moment, inches away from its neck. No matter how much he had pushed himself, the blade hadn’t moved an inch.
’A skill that can create an invisible force one and a half times the strength of the wielder.’
He could either use it to attack or defend.
Leon felt that if the monster had attacked him using this skill, he didn’t think it would have landed due to speed. However, if it had landed, he would have been in serious trouble.
Now he called out his status once again to see how high his stats were.
[Character Information]
[Name: Leon]
[Level: 6]
[Class: Elemental Paragon(SSS)]
[Age: 10 ( Soul Age: 26)]
[Race: Human]
[Cultivation: Apprentice Rank]
[Affinity: All (Rank 7)]
[Strength: 33]
[Agility: 34]
[Stamina: 34]
[Intelligence: 150]
[Skills: King’s Touch (Level 1- Epic), Lightning Bolt (Level 1 - Common)]
[Technique: Mana Body Enhancement(Adept Rank)]
’Holy cow, my stats are higher than my master’s.’
In terms of pure stats, not a single one of her stats was above his, especially Mana and Intelligence, which were high.
Leon tried to see more information about the skills he had just learned. When he had tried to do so in his hand earlier, it had failed to display it, but now it could be a different story.
He wasn’t wrong as two golden screens appeared in front of him.
[King’s Touch (Level 1 - Epic)]
[Mana cost: 50 Mana/Sec]
[Use: Let the user control an invisible force 1.5 times the strength of the wielder]
’Now I understand why the monster didn’t use this skill for long, considering how high the mana cost for the skill was.’
But for him, he could use this skill a few times during a battle to turn the tides. It wouldn’t have much effect on his reserves.
Now onto the next screen.
[Lightning Bolt (Level 1 - Common)]
[Mana cost: 5 Mana/Use]
[Use: Shoots a bolt of lightning]
’That’s a skill I could spam hundreds of times, but I feel like it wouldn’t be a strong attack.’
He had noticed the level of information of Seraphine’s skills. She had quite a few skills with levels higher than 50.
He didn’t need anyone to tell him what increasing the level might do. It would increase the strength of the skill.

He felt now he had nothing left to do other than grind. He had to learn to control his new strength too, along with increasing the level of new skills, while trying to learn to use the space element—at least trying to match his level of control with his ice element. The same could be said for the lightning element.

There was also one element he would like to delve into. It was Time. He had a feeling it would be hard to control that element, but he had the Rank 7 affinity with the passive ability he had gotten with his class. It would be a waste not to try it.
Especially since he could imagine it being broken.
’What if I just stopped the time for the opponent?’
’That’s gonna be a wild move. That would be helpful to me in the time of need.’
’I am gonna try my best. I have all the time in the world. I am gonna learn it no matter what.’

If he couldn’t do it today, then the next day or the day after that. One day for him inside his Dimensional Hourglass would be 1000 days, more than 2 and a half years. He believed he could do all these things in no time.

chapters.title: Chapter 52: Practicing New Element
paragraphs: Leon didn’t waste any more time thinking and entered his time dimension after sitting in a more comfortable cross-legged position on the ground.
The steps he took from the floor, were only a few steps, but they felt heavy and filled with power.
Thud
Thud
Quite a bit of noise was created due to his controlled steps hitting the wooden floor. He was putting his feet down gently, fearing he would break the floor.

After taking his position, his consciousness entered the same timeless expanse of grey. The first time he entered here to train, it felt so boring from time to time, to just train for days with his dagger.
But he was getting used to this space. He could even feel a bit excited to enter this place because he knew when he came out, he would be much stronger than before.
A thought arose in his mind before he even started training.
’Let’s see if this works in here too...’
He called out for his status screen in his mind to see if it would work in this form or not. He had never tried it and was curious to find out.
’Status’
Those commands in his mind made a shimmering transparent golden screen appear in front of his mystical eyes.
[Character Information]
[Name: Leon]
[Level: 4]
[Class: Elemental Paragon(SSS)]
[Age: 10 ( Soul Age: 26)]
[Race: Human]
[Cultivation: Apprentice Rank]
[Affinity: All (Rank 7)]
[Strength: 33]
[Agility: 34]
[Stamina: 34]
[Intelligence: 150]
[Skills: King’s Touch (Level 1- Epic), Lightning Bolt (Level 1 - Common)]
[Technique: Mana Body Enhancement(Adept Rank)]

Seeing the rank 7 elemental affinity, he felt delighted. He knew if this ability was in the hands of others, it wouldn’t have been as potent as with him, as he held the affinity to all the elements. This ability or this class felt like it was made just for him.

The fact it didn’t even take any toll on him at all in any form when he activated the passive was even more amazing. After the first activation, it felt like it had become a part of him. He didn’t need to do anything to stay in that way. He could feel he could turn it off, but why would he.
The connection between him and the elements was stronger than ever.
’Let’s start with my lightning affinity control, reaching at least the same level as Ice affinity.’
Then he would focus on Space affinity. While skills sound cool and amazing, having control of your affinity and using it as you wish is much more practical than single skills.
So he knew which thing to give priority to.

He remembered it took him about four months to reach that level of control in both Ice and Wind elements. It was only because before, he had trained for more than a year inside this space to reach his Mana Body reinforcement to Adept rank, which had improved his Mana control to a high degree.

Leon started now. He tried to summon a bit of lightning around his hand while using only a little mana. He got it summoned on the first try, which was a bit surprising, like how he wanted it to go, but it was like a wild untamed beast without control.
Crackle!
For the little amount of mana he had used, it was also surprising to see his whole forearm being covered in yellow lightning, crackling with dangerous intensity.
’The increase in rank in affinity had reduced the cost of mana, and more importantly, made the element many times stronger than before.’
He got a bit curious as he wanted to see how powerful it was. He tried to use about 100 mana but didn’t go as far as before like using about 250 mana while creating the spear.
He didn’t think he could shape it in the form he wanted or compress it to make it more powerful, so he used the raw power.

He was standing in a rocky area. He never focused much on the world formed inside the hourglass before, but everything felt too real. It didn’t feel like it was made out of his imagination, as he had never visited a place like this.

As far as he could see, there were only grey rocky mountains around, and beyond that, his sight couldn’t allow him to see. He was surrounded by them. There was no sun and moon in here, but it was always around the time before sunset.
He activated his adept rank mana body enhancement and tried to run toward a big rock that seemed a perfect target for his trial.
Boom!

A boom sound was made due to the pressure he had caused to the wind around him. His body moved so fast that he had no control over it. A cloud of dust was left in the place he stood a second ago, and now his body was a hundred meters away on the ground with a few broken bones and blood leaking out of his hands and legs.
Crash!
"Gah—damn it!" he growled through gritted teeth, the pain flaring like fire along his limbs.

It reminded him a bit about the time inside the dungeon against the thorn monster, as that was the only thing that hurt him to that degree. It wasn’t at that level, but broken bones could be such a big liability in the real world.
’It’s good I didn’t try anything in the real world.’
But this experience made him realize one absolute rule and two important things as his body got back to its original state after a few seconds.
’Absolute rule: Never scratch your balls no matter how much itches when using lighting affinity, that shit fucking hurts!’
While recovering he had done that and it was even more painful than the crash itself.
Recovery was just as painful as the crash, as everything would mend itself like going back to the previous state in real-time with the same pain.
First, how awesome this treasure was. He understood how powerful a mythical ranked treasure was. It could change the fate of the person.
’The grumpiness in the entity’s voice was justified when I got this treasure.’

Second, he needed an element that could heal his wounds in case of injuries. He was getting stronger much faster than he had thought. His own strength could finish him with a slight mishap. He did feel tougher than before but not to the degree that he could take the brunt of his own attacks.
He was lucky to have this treasure, which would allow him to run wild and make his learning process much faster. Otherwise, it would have been much tougher to train.

chapters.title: Chapter 53: Choosing a new Element?
paragraphs: ’But which element, I could think of only three elements: light, life, or holy. Their mention was in the book of Lin Fang, all three of them were rare elements.’
But when he thought of them he felt a strong connection to each of them like every other element—they were waiting for him to just master them.

However, he had read that to use holy elements, one had to borrow the power through a connection with god. He didn’t know about any gods and even if he knew he didn’t want to entangle himself with it.
With holy elements, he did have the ability to heal but through his connection with the divine, he would create what the church called miracles. That was what he read about it.

Still, if that was the case wouldn’t that element be a waste of time for him? He didn’t think about it much now. Once he traveled to higher realms he would try to find information on them so he could learn how to use this holy element which was said to be one of the most powerful elements against undeads.

As for the light element, it would do some minor healing, and was said to have powerful attacks and even was used for increasing speed. It was a versatile element, which was why Lin Fang said it was one of the strongest elements.

The Life element which he had chosen to master was said to be related to vitality. It was the ideal element for healing, regrowing arms, broken bones—everything, which those other two elements would struggle with, light and then holy which was said to be borrowed power that Lin Fang described.
He didn’t like the way it sounded.
If he was gonna use holy elements, he wanted to be the source of his own power, created by his own mana, not some so-called miracle created by the connection of some god.
The life element was even said to restore people from the brink of the dead if someone had enough mana and control over the element.

’I had started to realize that little by little I was increasing the amount of elements I would master. I did have all the elements. I had the time because of my treasure, so why not? But one at a time and at my own pace. I would master all elements one day in the future.’
’I didn’t even know if I was aware of all the elements in the world.’
’Now I needed to master Lightning, Space, Life, and then Time, which I would try to, at least reach at the same level as my Ice and Wind Elements.’

Getting up from the ground first for a few hours he practiced to control his strength, by running, jumping, punching, and various types of things including the use of mana body enhancement little by little.

It took him about 8 hours to get used to his own strength with or without the use of mana. Now this time he used the same mana enhancement in his body. With a boom he vanished from his spot, leaving only dust, and reached the rock thrice the size of his which was supposed to be the target for his lightning magic practice.

He had learned from experience that to use any element, it would need his mental power which was the term he learned from Lin Fang, which he said was the intelligence stat. The more imagination power the easier it was for you to cast a bigger and more destructive attack.

But for control over elements, there were no shortcuts. He had to train for months to learn to compress ice and wind, like using wind to enhance his speed. It required precise control over the element. One mishap and instead of increasing your own speed through wind, you would stumble during a fight. A death wish in serious scenarios against monsters.
He started using his mana. Using his will he tried to create a lightning bolt to hit the target rock. It was wild and untamed. He could feel the element. He more or less used 100 mana in this attack.
It took only a few seconds as a huge lightning bolt the size of 10 meters struck with a thunderous sound.
Boom.

The destruction caused by it was something that he hadn’t anticipated fully. Two meters of rocky surface got torn apart, black burning marks on the ground, but he didn’t land on the rock he had targeted but instead right next to it on the ground.

He deflected the chunk of shattered ground that tried to hit him using his shield made out of Ice element. It would have been easier to deflect it using the wind element and just change the direction, but he had chosen to show the Ice element in public so he was focusing more on it.
In terms of sheer destruction, he believed this lightning bolt had come quite close to the spear he had created before, using more than twice the mana before.

Which he believed to be the effect of the increase in the rank of elemental affinity, and the fact he used two elements to make that attack focusing only on destruction, and even then this simple raw thunder came close to it, surprised him quite a lot.
’Hell, I am starting to become strong.’
This thought came as a realization to him, but he didn’t give it much thought and continued focusing on practicing his element.
It started with hours and it turned to days and a month.

A month was the amount of time it took for Leon to master the Lightning affinity at the same level as his Ice element, but he didn’t stop as it had happened quite faster than he had imagined. He had thought it would take two months for him to reach that level so he decided to continue.

He trained for an extra month, focusing on using as much amount of mana as he could to create powerful attacks made out of compressed lightning. This method of practice would focus both on his control over the element and at the same time increase and sharpen his mental imagination, as he found out that having over 1000 mana didn’t mean he would create an attack using 1000 mana.

He realized once he reached the 350 mark that was where his limit lay. The mana went out of his control. The creation would go out of control, either by self-destruction if he wasn’t fast enough or just dissipate if he was careful.

The first time that happened, he almost got turned to ashes because of this. 350 mana with his rank 7 affinity, and it was the time when his attack wasn’t controlled. That massive blast of pure destruction even when in the last second he forced a shield out of Ice around him.
The result.

Ice shield didn’t even last for a second. His body got burned. He was flung away losing both his arms and one of his legs gone, punctured lungs, sizzling muscle. He would have died after a few minutes in real scenarios, but he got healed back to his previous state in a minute, but that pain was torturous.
He screamed in agony.
Trying to remember about it gave chills to his body.

He didn’t like the way it sounded.
If he was gonna use holy elements, he wanted to be the source of his own power, created by his own mana, not some so-called miracle created by the connection of some god.
The life element was even said to restore people from the brink of the dead if someone had enough mana and control over the element.
’I had started to realize that little by little I was increasing the amount of elements I would master.
I did have all the elements.
I had the time because of my treasure, so why not?
But one at a time and at my own pace.
I would master all elements one day in the future.’
’I didn’t even know if I was aware of all the elements in the world.’
’Now I needed to master Lightning, Space, Life, and then Time, which I would try to, at least reach at the same level as my Ice and Wind Elements.’

Getting up from the ground first for a few hours he practiced to control his strength, by running, jumping, punching, and various types of things including the use of mana body enhancement little by little.
It took him about 8 hours to get used to his own strength with or without the use of mana.
Now this time he used the same mana enhancement in his body.
With a boom he vanished from his spot, leaving only dust, and reached the rock thrice the size of his which was supposed to be the target for his lightning magic practice.
He had learned from experience that to use any element, it would need his mental power which was the term he learned from Lin Fang, which he said was the intelligence stat.
The more imagination power the easier it was for you to cast a bigger and more destructive attack.
But for control over elements, there were no shortcuts.
He had to train for months to learn to compress ice and wind, like using wind to enhance his speed.
It required precise control over the element.
One mishap and instead of increasing your own speed through wind, you would stumble during a fight.
A death wish in serious scenarios against monsters.
He started using his mana.
Using his will he tried to create a lightning bolt to hit the target rock.
It was wild and untamed.
He could feel the element.
He more or less used 100 mana in this attack.
It took only a few seconds as a huge lightning bolt the size of 10 meters struck with a thunderous sound.
Boom.
The destruction caused by it was something that he hadn’t anticipated fully.
Two meters of rocky surface got torn apart, black burning marks on the ground, but he didn’t land on the rock he had targeted but instead right next to it on the ground.
He deflected the chunk of shattered ground that tried to hit him using his shield made out of Ice element.
It would have been easier to deflect it using the wind element and just change the direction, but he had chosen to show the Ice element in public so he was focusing more on it.
In terms of sheer destruction, he believed this lightning bolt had come quite close to the spear he had created before, using more than twice the mana before.

Which he believed to be the effect of the increase in the rank of elemental affinity, and the fact he used two elements to make that attack focusing only on destruction, and even then this simple raw thunder came close to it, surprised him quite a lot.
’Hell, I am starting to become strong.’
This thought came as a realization to him, but he didn’t give it much thought and continued focusing on practicing his element.
It started with hours and it turned to days and a month.
A month was the amount of time it took for Leon to master the Lightning affinity at the same level as his Ice element, but he didn’t stop as it had happened quite faster than he had imagined.
He had thought it would take two months for him to reach that level so he decided to continue.
He trained for an extra month, focusing on using as much amount of mana as he could to create powerful attacks made out of compressed lightning.

This method of practice would focus both on his control over the element and at the same time increase and sharpen his mental imagination, as he found out that having over 1000 mana didn’t mean he would create an attack using 1000 mana.
He realized once he reached the 350 mark that was where his limit lay.
The mana went out of his control.
The creation would go out of control, either by self-destruction if he wasn’t fast enough or just dissipate if he was careful.
The first time that happened, he almost got turned to ashes because of this.
350 mana with his rank 7 affinity, and it was the time when his attack wasn’t controlled.
That massive blast of pure destruction even when in the last second he forced a shield out of Ice around him.
The result.
Ice shield didn’t even last for a second.
His body got burned.
He was flung away losing both his arms and one of his legs gone, punctured lungs, sizzling muscle.
He would have died after a few minutes in real scenarios, but he got healed back to his previous state in a minute, but that pain was torturous.
He screamed in agony.
Trying to remember about it gave chills to his body.

chapters.title: Chapter 54: Mysterious presence and comprehending elements.
paragraphs: If he had to worship something, instead of the god, he would throw an offering of his only mythical ranked treasure. It was just so good.

After the mortifying incident, he was careful while using mana at higher levels. His limit started to increase in the past month. Now he could control 500 mana at the same time. He had to be careful, as after 550 it was like asking to be blasted to oblivion.

A spear hovered above Leon. Its size was much smaller than the ice spear he had created twice his height. It was just a bit larger than a normal spear, bright yellow. Only thin golden yellow lightning crackled around it, Despite its small size, the air trembled from the mere presence of the spear.
Crackle!

His mystical eyes locked onto the small rocky mountain 100 meters away from him. This attack could be said to be his most powerful attack—an accumulation of wild lightning worth 500 mana, condensed into the form of a spear.

He launched the attack with his mind. The speed was so fast that just as he launched it, it felt like it got teleported to its target. There were no loud noises before it hit the target, only the faint hum in the air.
BOOOOM!!!
After the collision, for a moment there was only a small light, but it got bigger and bigger, along with an ear-shattering boom. Leon was watching everything with a glint of excitement in his eyes.
The small mountain was getting obliterated.

The large rocks were blasted at incredible speed. He blocked all of them with precision. With excitement, for some of the bigger ones instead of creating a bigger ice shield, he just used his mana to enhance his body and punched them hard to shatter them into pieces.
A glove made out of compressed ice protected his hands from getting even a scratch.
After the dust settled, the mountain was nowhere to be seen. Only broken rocks remained of different sizes, along with a big crater he had formed.
He couldn’t help but laugh out loud, seeing the destruction he had caused.
"Hahahaa That was amazing!"
Somewhere inside Leon’s dimensional space, inside an unknown place, two mysterious eyes opened, their color shimmering white.
An ethereal voice sounded into the void.

"Hehehe Master is so talented this time. I had never seen anything like him or heard about it. He is such a monster, hehehe shattering mountains in apprentice rank. What is he, a True dragon? So cool. I wonder how much mana he has. He didn’t get exhausted after that attack. So cool. Once I meet him, it’s gonna be so awesome."

"Hmph! It’s good that the lame man left. He wasn’t even qualified to be in my presence. Can’t even detect my presence being a prime divinity. Lame loser! But the new master seems to have a strong affinity to time. I feel it. Surely he would be able to fulfill the conditions."

"But I wonder how many affinities he has. I have seen he has 4, including time which I could feel because of my affinity and connection with this realm. As for the others, I can only judge based on what I see."
"He has surpassed 99% of geniuses of the universe with that alone, as his affinity is either rank 6 or rank 7, especially when he has Time affinity."
Suddenly it got angry remember how it got trapped here.

"That fucking bastard calling himself The Keeper of the Dimension, cringy fucker! He trapped me here, saying I was too dangerous to roam the Universe. He did win against me, hmph! It makes me so mad!!! Still, I would be free when the condition set by him is met."
"Hehe, how many years it has been. It was diabolical to think great me would have to serve someone else even after being free, if by some miracle, but it seems a worthy master is here."
"Soon I would be able to roam the outside world with the master, hehe!"
"Hopefully he won’t die before that."
Leon was satisfied with his control over his lightning element now, which was even more than his ice element.

A little more than 2 months had passed inside, which would mean not even 2 hours had passed in the outside world. So he still had so much time to practice. It would be around 2 hours more, then he had to go for lunch. He had refused the maid for breakfast as he wasn’t feeling much hungry.

But he did feel like his real body was a bit hungry now. Still, he could endure it for 2 more hours. When this body was once used to surviving a day with single bread or even completely hungry, he wasn’t aware of his memory at that time, but they were all his own memories.

He had around a little more than 2 hours, which means around 3 months here. He would like to train his space element, one of the powerful and mysterious elements. He had the memory of the dungeon gate. He was excited when he felt the connection that time. It was made using space elements.
’If I could create portals, that would be so overpowered, but that’s not for now. I have to focus on simple things first.’
For a moment, his mind didn’t work as he wondered how he should go about learning this new yet complex element.
He started by recalling how he had learned all his previous elements, instead of jumping into it right away.

’Ice, my first element, which I used mana to create ice for the first time. But how is it that I created it in a few tries? It could be said it must be due to my Rank 5 affinity at that time, but he felt that was not entirely true.’

’I understood ice to some degree. It was just water at a very low temperature, meaning solid form, and water is that. Even if I didn’t go into the scientific terms of my previous world like how it was made of H2O atoms.’
He knew how it tastes, and how it feels. He understood water to some degree.

He believed in having the imagination of water, say even ice, same for air and lightning, which was just an electrostatic discharge caused by different electrical charge points or regions, like between clouds and ground, or it could be between two different clouds too.
’In lightning, my scientific knowledge helped me, even if I didn’t think about it before, but deep down I was aware of it.’

’But it raised a question for me once again. While I have this scientific knowledge due to my interest in science and being from a world where this type of knowledge was common, how about the people of this world? How about master? How can she control lightning? She had even reached level 1 Aura in lightning. What is it that she has that I didn’t have?’
For a moment image of her beautiful appearance in her formal attire arose in his mind, the thought made him blush for a few seconds.
He took a few deep breaths and continued with his training to learn new elements.
’Focus!!!’

’My control over lightning is quite good, but I have no idea what even Aura is. I didn’t even get some feeling of reaching closer to it. It is the truth of the element, that is the concept, that fundamental of Aura.’
’Didn’t I know the truth about how lightning is created already?’
Leon felt confused for the first time, stuck between science and how elements are being made.

chapters.title: Chapter 55: Discovering Applications of Space Element?
paragraphs: Chapter 55: Discovering Applications of Space Elements?
Leon took a deep breath to calm his mind, then removed these distracting thoughts for now. But if he had the chance, he would like to know from his master how she had learned lightning Aura.

He knew what space elements could do, like teleportation, moving objects from one space to another, portals, and the inventory that seems to be made using space elements which he could detect because of his high-ranked affinity.
So he had some ideas about where to start, throwing away the thought about the truth of the element which distracted him for a while.

He had little more than three months left inside, which would be about two and a half hours, a little less but he had around that time before the maid might knock on his door for lunch together with master.

He started his training by first trying to detect everything around him using his space element. He used a bit of his mana to send his spatial energy 5 meters around him, which he learned to create after a few tries.

Around a five-meter radius of him, he could detect the smallest of things. If he focused enough, he could even count the 193 pieces of medium-sized rocks around him caused due to his punching the big rock earlier.

He knew that along with his intelligence stat, the capacity of his brain at which it processes information and his memory had increased to an absurd degree. But seeing it firsthand with his spatial affinity, he knew this would be a terrifying ability that would leave him with no blind spots.
He decided to give it a name, calling it spatial awareness because of how it suits it.
For two whole weeks, he played around with his spatial awareness, trying to see where his limit lies along with improving his control over his element which was just the derivative of this practice.
The Results.
Leon had found that he could spread his spatial awareness around a hundred-meter radius of him. If he goes over, the information would start to overload his brain, resulting in headaches and nausea.

The mana cost was quite steep too. This was the first time he felt he had not nearly enough mana. He had to spend 100 mana per second if he would like to maintain spatial awareness over 100 meters around him.

For now, he didn’t think it was wise for him to use it that way, so he had decided he could use it for spatial awareness over 100 meters in a burst only for 1 second to collect all the information around him. It would be quite useful even when he couldn’t get live info on moving objects if they were around him.

But for fights, he could maintain spatial awareness around the 5-meter radius of himself, costing 3 mana per second only. As the larger the area, he had to spend more mana to control the element. He knew over time, with better control over the element, the cost of mana would decrease.
’In 5 meters radius now I would have no blind spots.’

The spatial he used was in a spherical form around him, which other people couldn’t see, he chose this shape because it felt most natural and useful, even if the attack came from underground he couldn’t detect it.
’Saying no blind spots wasn’t just for show’
It may sound not a big thing, but Leon knew it would make him overpowered in close combat and long-range attacks too if he was fast enough to dodge them, even if he didn’t see them coming.

In the past week, Leon did gain control over the space element, and he felt satisfied with his current progress on spatial awareness. So he now moved to his next idea, which was to move objects from one place to another using his spatial control.
’If I gained high enough control and have full confidence over it, I would be able to teleport myself for short distances.’
For the next 3 months, Leon focused on trying to master the ability to move objects from one distance to another.

And one more thing to consider—in this space, Leon doesn’t get tired, hungry, or need to sleep, so 3 months could be said to be six months, and it could be the same for every other training he had done previously.

He trained and trained continuously, not just doing repetition as it’s just stupid, he used his creativity to try to learn new things and try different approaches trying to find more uses for the element.
3 months had passed.
Even after that period of time had passed, Leon wasn’t confident enough to try to teleport himself. It might result in half his body being torn to pieces because of his lack of control.

While he wasn’t able to learn to teleport, his time wasn’t wasted. The cost of mana for 100 meters of spatial awareness had reduced to 70 mana per second, and for a 5-meter radius around him, it was as low as between 1 to 2 mana per second, being closer to two.

But that was just due to his increase in control. He had learned to transport rocks the size of bigger footballs around 10 meters from him without any problem. It wasn’t instant—it would take him 1 to 2 seconds to do that.

Unlike the attacks he did with other elements like ice and thunder, where in less than half a second he would attack because of his practice, he did try to reduce the time with constant practice. But in the given time, that was the most he could do because of how harder it was to control this element compared to others.
Still, this was not the most fruitful thing he gained in the practice, as he had learned two new applications of the spatial element which he named Spatial Lock and Spatial Distortion.

Both of these abilities he considered top-notch because of how useful they are. While learning to transport the rock from distance A to B, they would most of the time get destroyed, so he thought why not just use this as a form of attack, instead of trying to control it and make it more chaotic.

He didn’t even have to calculate the distance, size, or any other calculations. Just choose a point in space and make that space chaotic. When using this ability, the space he would distort would become a chaotic mass of destruction, obliterating what was present there.
It would look like there was swirling space.

He didn’t know how someone could defend against such an attack. He could create spatial distortion maximum to the size of a football anywhere within a ten-meter radius of him, taking about 1 to 2 seconds to do it but closer to one not two in this case due to its less difficulty.
While it might seem overpowered, he wasn’t confident he would land it on a moving target. Trained fighters have instincts hardened by battle to danger—they would dodge this attack.
Still, he wasn’t worried. If he trained more and reached a point so that he could create distortion almost instantly, that would be terrifying to anyone who faces it.

chapters.title: Chapter 56: A Bet?
paragraphs: Next was the spatial lock, in which he would freeze the space from moving around a place. He had nothing to test it on, so he was his own test subject. If it was something like teleportation, he would not have tried it on himself even in this immortal form.
Because some parts of rock would just disappear—he doesn’t know where—in failed attempts of teleportation, which scared him to try it on himself even here.

When the rocks travel from point A to point B to reach the distance instantly, they travel through a separate space where the space is much closer. It made him understand the concept of how the portal works, and at the same time how dangerous it was.

But freezing the space was much easier. It didn’t take control and focus on that level. He just had to make the existing space stay as it was by forcing it using his spatial element. The limit of the size of the football doesn’t apply to it because of its lower complexity. He can freeze a regular-sized human in place using this ability easily.

Still, the cons were the same. It took him to focus to cast, around 1.2 seconds, which for a monster like the thrown monster would be enough to sense the danger, but dodging it might be harder because of the larger space and only a little time. If he planned it well at the right moment, even a powerful enemy would be vulnerable for a few seconds—enough for him to finish it.

The strength of the space hold depends on how much mana he used. With 50 mana per couple of seconds used on himself, it took him about 2 seconds to break free using all his strength with mana body enhancement on its full power.
But if he used his lightning affinity to make a big burst of lightning around him at the same time and used everything before, he could break free almost instantly.

But it would take him about 30 mana to do everything. This amount of mana was one-fourth of a normal level 10 apprentice, and if experiencing it for the first time, they might not even be able to escape that quickly.

However, this was only when he limited himself to 50 mana usage to hold the enemy for a few seconds. He had so much mana—why would he limit himself in a proper fight? He would end it as fast as possible if the enemy was strong.
As for most people, he doesn’t even think he would need to use his space element at all.
He hasn’t even tried to make combo attacks with ice and lightning. He knew they were going to be devastating, but it would be for a later time, as he felt like he had to leave for lunch now.
He wasn’t where he liked to be, as he was still close to his goal for the space element, and he hadn’t even started with the life element and skills he had to level up to.
Still, it was a fruitful endeavor considering only 4 hours had passed in the outside world.

His consciousness came out of the dimension with just a thought. He looked at the clock—there were still 5 minutes left before the maid might come to take him. He decided to play around with his space element for the time being, using spatial energy around his room to teleport small objects. At first, it felt weird, but only after doing it a couple of times, did he get accustomed to it.
Knock Knock
Hearing the knock on the door, he walked up to the door and opened it. Instead of any maid, he found Kaela, Seraphine’s most trusted knight, standing at the door.
He didn’t wait for her to tell him anything and said instead.
"Let’s go. The commander must be waiting for me at the dining table."
In response, Kaela answered instantly and started leading him.
"As you wish, young master Leon."
He glanced at her for a moment as she seemed to recognize him even after the change.
"Hmm. So you know, Kaela."
Kaela, leading him, answered him.

"Of course, it wasn’t hard for me to notice it, young master. Despite being taller and much older-looking in appearance, you resemble your previous self quite a lot. And it’s not just me—most of the staff inside the mansion must have realized it too. But in their mind, they would find it hard to believe this fact as you look much older after only a few days, and your strange eyes must also be confusing to them."

Leon heard her. He hadn’t had much contact with her before, only talked to her a couple of times over the course of three years, but he didn’t know she was this talkative. But what she said was true indeed.
"You are right, Kaela. They think I am my own older brother." He paused for a moment and asked her with curiosity this time.
"What do you think Master would do about this?"
She almost answered him instantly, as she seemed happy to answer him.
"Of course, my lady would tell everyone that you are the same young master Leon from before, and your class awakening had caused these changes."

Despite hearing her confident tone, Leon doesn’t seem to think what she said would happen, because he doesn’t think it was a common thing for people to age 5 years in a few days just because of their class awakening.
"I think you are wrong, Kaela, on this one."

Kaela heard him, and she didn’t think it was weird for him to think that way, because he didn’t know how loyal all the people under her were to her. They could even give up their lives if it was for her, and it was the same for her.

She doesn’t know why, but Leon felt different from when she had seen him today entering her lady’s office. She couldn’t tell what it was, but he was different in some way even if he looked the same. It was just her intuition, but she didn’t give it much thought.

For she had a plan to make her lady even more happy. She did have become much happiness after Leon’s arrival, but the more happy she would be, the more accomplished Kaela would feel in her duty as her knight.
"Why don’t we make a bet about this, young master Leon?"
"A bet?" Leon exclaimed. While he doesn’t think he would lose, she does seem quite confident, which makes him cautious.
"If it’s a bet, what’s going to be on the stakes?"
"Hmm, for my end it’s not going to be something hard for you to do, but if you win, I will give you one gold coin."
’One Gold Coin’

If it was before exchanging his wealth, he would have scoffed at her, but right now 1 gold coin was a very enticing amount for him. He didn’t want to give up on it when it was such easy money, but he added a condition just to be cautious.
"I won’t do anything that would harm me even in the slightest, and if I deem what you’re asking to be too much for one gold coin, I would reject your demand."

chapters.title: Chapter 57: A Loyal Knight and an important realization
paragraphs: Kaela looked at him strangely for a moment, as if he were setting conditions like she might ask for his life or send him to infiltrate enemy territory.

It irritated her more than she expected. She knew he had spent his childhood in an environment where trusting others was nearly impossible, but she had hoped that by now, he’d put more faith in those around him. It saddened her that, even briefly, he thought she might harm him.

"Fine, young master Leon," she said, keeping her tone measured. "But you should try to trust people more—especially those who care deeply for you. Like my lady... or even me. I would never betray her, and certainly not someone she holds so dear." She paused, her voice softening. "I can say with confidence that my lady considers you family. She has no one else besides you. Please, don’t hurt her just because your past made it hard to trust. Try to give her a little more of your faith."
Her voice wasn’t commanding—it felt more like a plea. A heartfelt request from someone who genuinely cared.
Then Kaela did something unexpected. She bowed. It was something she reserved solely for Seraphine. But if it could bring her lady happiness, she would do anything to make it possible.

She knew just how kind her lady was, beneath that tough, distant exterior. Seraphine helped those in need not for recognition but because she couldn’t bear the idea of someone losing a loved one like she had. Despite her achievements, she led a lonely life, giving no time to herself. That only changed when Leon arrived. From a monotonous, cold existence, Seraphine had begun to smile—just a little—and Kaela had noticed the warmth that slowly returned to her.

As her knight, Kaela had believed that obeying every command and being willing to lay down her life was enough. But watching her lady change made her realize something else—being the perfect knight meant more than duty. It meant doing whatever it took to make her happy too, just like she’d done for others.
Leon stood silent, listening to every word. He had seen her bow—this woman he barely paid attention to before—and he couldn’t bring himself to speak.
’’Do I trust Seraphine completely?’

He wanted to say yes. And maybe he did, in part. But deep down, caution had become second nature. No matter who it was. He felt guilty for lying to her so often, though he told himself it was for both their safety. Truthfully, it was fear. Habit. A defense mechanism he’d clung to for far too long.
He felt closer to her than anyone else in the world, but even then... the caution remained. Maybe it came from seven years of surviving the slums. Maybe from a life once lived on Earth. Maybe both.
’Does it really matter now? Things aren’t the same anymore.’

Kaela noticed the distant look in his eyes. They had both stopped walking. Her next words might seem harsh, but she had to speak them. If it was for her lady, she couldn’t stay silent. Seraphine had found something like a new family, and Kaela wouldn’t let it fall apart just because someone failed to notice the cracks forming.
Her voice sharpened.

"You know, young master Leon, if you had set those same conditions with her directly—as part of a bet—it would’ve crushed her. Just the thought that you believe she might hurt you... it’s heartbreaking. For her, family means everything. More than you probably realize. And she’s more vulnerable than you think."
Kaela truly believed that. Seraphine would be devastated to hear it. And though Kaela knew she was being harsh with someone who was still, in many ways, a child, she told herself it was for the best.

Each word struck deeper than the last. The idea of Seraphine being heartbroken disturbed Leon more than he expected. Memories rushed back—her holding him after a nightmare, taking care of him when he was sick, even cooking for him once or twice. He’d always assumed it was just to make him more willing to join her command.

But yesterday, she revealed something that unsettled him. That those born in this world from people who can use magic had a natural advantage thanks to their ability to use mana. She didn’t know his secret—that his power came from the treasure. Compared to the girl he had seen in the dungeon before merging with the orb, he was still weaker.
She hadn’t been kind to him just because he was talented. He had realized it somewhere in his mind, but never truly accepted it.
Now it hit him hard. His personality—so cautious, so guarded—might actually end up hurting the people he had begun to care for. If he didn’t change, it would only get worse.
’I don’t know how things will go from now on, but I have to start being more honest with the person who cares this much for me. I can’t let her get hurt because of me.’
He looked at Kaela—the knight he had never given much thought to until now—and spoke with sincerity.
"Thank you for making me realize all this, Kaela."
A genuine smile spread across her face. She pulled a coin from her pouch and placed it in his hand.
Leon looked down, surprised to see a gold coin. "Why are you giving me this, Kaela? I didn’t win the bet."
A smug little grin touched her lips. She felt satisfied with how things had turned out. The coin was a small price for what had been accomplished. Still, she answered.
"Just take it as my appreciation, young master. And forget the bet—it serves no purpose now."
’Serves no purpose? She might’ve just wanted to make me do something that brought me closer to Master. Kaela really does care about her.’

Leon didn’t argue. He slipped the coin into his pocket. He was poor, and turning down money wasn’t exactly an option. But more than that, he now felt Kaela was far more perceptive than he’d given her credit for. In hindsight, he probably would have lost that bet. Despite his logic, she had understood things he hadn’t.
Together, they resumed walking and entered the dining hall side by side.

chapters.title: Chapter 58: Opening up to Master
paragraphs: As soon as he reached the dining hall, he could see Seraphine taking the head seat of the hall, looking gorgeous without doing anything.

He had noticed for a moment that her eyes widened, and she had a shocked look on her face for the first time, but it was only for a second, and it went back to normal afterward. But it couldn’t escape his senses at all.
’So she noticed the change in my strength.’
He had tried to keep it under control, and it worked on Kaela but not on Seraphine.
’Hmm, but she didn’t say anything. It seems she was waiting for me to say it myself and reveal how it happened.’
He walked forward and naturally took the seat on the side right next to her, and Kaela didn’t accompany him there, having stopped at the door to stand guard.

Hot, steaming food was already presented on the table by the maids beforehand. He understood now that she did this because she wanted to have alone time—master and student—or, to put it better, family time, which he understood now.
He looked at the table and observed. No matter how many times he ate here, he couldn’t help but drool internally at the sight of it.

The table was set with quiet elegance, offering a refined but satisfying noble meal. Alongside the roast duck and grilled venison, there was spiced lamb on the bone, thin-sliced smoked boar, and a slow-cooked beef stew served in a deep silver bowl.
A warm rabbit pie rested near the center, its golden crust flaked open, and beside it, lemon-poached trout shimmered under the soft light.
Fresh bread—soft rolls, flatbreads, and cheese-filled buns—was laid out with herbed butter, fig jam, and garlic oil. Small dishes held pickled onions, spiced salt, and ground mustard.
Honey-glazed carrots, truffled mash, baked spinach, and lemon-grilled artichokes filled out the sides.
A modest cheese board sat at the edge, with dried fruits and roasted nuts. For dessert, berry tarts, honeyed dates, and almond cake gave a light finish.
Wine stood ready in a crystal decanter, and chilled mint water offered a clean touch. Balanced, tasteful, and fitting for a noble house that didn’t need to shout.
He didn’t show anything outwardly, as she had taught him noble etiquette—while beating him up—saying if he didn’t behave well as her student, it would tarnish both their images. So he did learn it.
Even with such a scrumptious meal in front of him, he didn’t start and instead looked directly into Seraphine’s eyes and said,
"Master, did you notice I have gotten stronger than before?"

Seraphine was a bit shocked that he revealed this fact himself without her asking. She was going to mention it after lunch—how could she not? She could feel that in just a couple of hours, Leon had become as strong as her. She couldn’t treat him lightly now, as if he were someone equal to her strength or even stronger. It had shocked her quite a bit when she first laid eyes on him at the end of the hall.

With her lightning Aura, which was a secret from everyone, there was no one else in her kingdom who had ever felt like this. The generals and the king’s special guards were strong, but if the worst came to the worst, she could defeat them with her lightning Aura. And most of the time, the feeling of threat wasn’t there when she met them. But in Leon’s case, she wasn’t sure of the outcome.
And she didn’t understand how this was possible. Despite her outer calm appearance, she was freaking out inside.

She could only nod in response to his words, as honesty was something she was expecting. She knew her disciple well in these few years and knew for a fact that he was the cautious type. Even in front of her, he would be cautious all the time.
It did make her sad that her openness in her feelings toward him over the past year hadn’t been able to change him, but after coming out of the dungeon, he was giving her more surprises than ever.

But she knew he was still hiding many things from her. Yet she never showed that she knew, because she didn’t want them to have differences and become separated because of it. He was her little disciple and her family. She couldn’t bring herself to be away from him now.
She was satisfied with whatever he would share with her and would never press him because of that. But she did hope they would have no secrets between them one day.
Leon couldn’t help but find her cute as she blankly nodded to his words, quite different from her composed commander front.
"Do you want me to tell you more about how I got stronger so quickly?"
Once again, she nodded cutely in response, looking quite eager to know. He couldn’t help but say it out loud.
"Master, you look so cute right now, haha."
Seraphine was genuinely baffled and caught off guard. Because he was being so open with her, she had acted a bit out of character.
But her years of being a commander had taught her to become composed at any moment. Still, she pouted for a bit and replied,

"I didn’t know my disciple would be the one to make the first move." Usually, she would be the one to tease him first, but not anymore. She liked the change quite a bit, even if it made her feel a bit weird.
"Do you want to know, Master?"

"Of course I want to know everything about my Leon," she said, and while saying that, she gave him a short hug, making him a bit breathless for a moment as she squeezed his face tightly into her bosom.
Leon was quite used to this, but he enjoyed the embrace now and felt relaxed. The fact that she lovingly called him her Leon made him want to be real with her.

There was no one else inside, so it was safe to have a conversation here. He trusted her fully now. He was still the same cautious Leon from before—but not in front of her, who clearly loved him so much.
Kaela had even told him that Seraphine had no one besides him. She didn’t explain more, which he was grateful for, as he would like to hear it from Master herself someday.

"Master, I don’t think you really are curious about how I got this strong. Forget it. I thought you would like to know, but it seems you’re more interested in teasing me."

Seraphine, hearing his words, paused in her tracks. It was a very difficult choice for her to make, as it had become hard for her to embarrass her disciple after the first few times she showered him with affection. He had become a bit immune to her hugs with his grumpy remarks.

The blush on his handsome face made her want to hug him more, but the fact that he was being honest with her—she didn’t want to miss that opportunity either. She was stuck, only for a split second, before she made a decision.
She once again embraced him in a hug much tighter than before, as she couldn’t control herself when he looked so inviting.
"My dear disciple, if you really don’t like it, just pull away from my hug. I won’t do it again." Her voice sounded a bit childish, as if she had done it intentionally.
Leon, hearing her childish voice, couldn’t understand how a commander like her could throw so many antics.

He did feel the warm and fuzzy feeling from her hug, but it wasn’t like before, when in his mind, while he hugged her, the constant thought played that she was doing this only to get something from him.

He knew her love was genuine, and so was her hug. It made him feel a bit weird. Even before, when he had reciprocated her hug, feeling her slim waist stirred different emotions toward her. He had ignored it then, but if he kept going like this, he knew it would be bad for his heart.

But he couldn’t pull away now, not after her words had made it hard for him, as it would indicate he didn’t like her hug, which would make her feel bad. He didn’t want that. But he had understood one thing—his master was playing around with him a bit too much.
’What if I can’t pull away from the hug? How about doing something that would make her pull away?’
He had one idea that would definitely work. She considered him as her family. She would definitely stop hugging him; otherwise, he could already imagine being hugged for half an hour.
’Let’s do this.’

It was only his head squished against her soft chest, and a bit of his upper body was hugged by her. With a smooth maneuver of his body, he slid out of his chair without breaking the hug and stood in front of her chair.

The chair was a luxurious one with no armrests, perfect for dining and also perfect for what he was about to do. Right now, he was in an awkward position, his knees bent slightly to match her hug. He was now five feet six inches, not that short.
It was a bold and embarrassing move, but he had to do it to escape from thirty minutes of being constantly hugged by her on and off, as if he were a plushie.
Seraphine was a bit curious about what he was doing while still in the hug, but she didn’t pay much attention to it. Right now, she had to focus more on the comforting hug that was melting her away.

Suddenly, he let his weight fall onto her lap. She had to adjust the hug so now his face reached her collarbone. But that wasn’t all—his body was now pressed against her. She was in her formal attire; she could feel everything. But instead of making her feel awkward, it awakened her instinct more to hug her cute disciple, who was being so nice today.

She smelled him as usual, taking large whiffs of his familiar sweet scent. It was almost addictive to her. Her hug was even tighter now, and knowing he had around the same physical strength as her—or even more—she didn’t have to worry about controlling her strength in this loving moment and could enjoy it fully.
Leon could feel her body all along his front, her softness on his shoulder, and her arms around him in a tight embrace. Instead of making her embarrassed, it backfired on him even more.
"Hehe, I didn’t know my disciple loved me so much that he had become so forward now. It seems the dungeon made my cute disciple realize how precious his master is. Hehe."

He felt quite lucky that she wasn’t able to see his face right now. Feeling how hot his cheeks were, he knew he was red as a tomato. If it were something else—like how much she loved him or how cute he was—it wouldn’t have had as much effect on him.
But instead, her words had too much truth in them to ignore. They made him feel too embarrassed, and the next words made him almost bite his own tongue for a second.
"It seems my lovely disciple is feeling shy right now and doesn’t want to answer me. Don’t worry—Master would be satisfied if you let me hug you as much as you want."

"But disciple, I’m not forcing you or anything. If you want, you can leave the hug. If you don’t like Master’s hugs, I’ll sit in the office afterward with boring paperwork and feel sad about how my only precious disciple doesn’t like me."

chapters.title: Chapter 62: Craziness and Shock
paragraphs: "I am s—"

His voice was louder than hers as he hurriedly replied to her. He knew what she was about to say. It made him feel that his master was not fully crazy—definitely some sense in her—but she didn’t have to say sorry, as he was the one who pushed her to the limit, and her reaction was a bit unexpected. But the fact he did like it—still, he wasn’t going to mention that to her.
"I am feeling perfectly fine! You don’t have to—don’t you have to say anything. Just keep quiet and finish lunch. It’s hard for me to talk right now."
Seraphine, hearing him, smiled gleefully, as it seemed that he didn’t dislike what happened between them, but he was just embarrassed, right? She knew how he was.

"Leon, if you don’t mind, I can help you in anything. We are family, after all." This was the first time she had openly mentioned being a family to him. Her eyes had a deep swirl in them and a small smile on her face.
Leon had only looked at her for a moment, and now he could see the deep swirl in her eyes, which he felt if he looked in them long enough, he would be swallowed whole.
What shocked him wasn’t her eyes but the words that had left her mouth, which she uttered while glancing toward his crotch.
He shivered slightly in his seat.
’Master is crazy.’
’In what world does family help out in things like that?’
’She has finally lost it!’
He knew it now—no amount of words would change his mind after seeing the way she had acted today.
He slammed the fork down on the table. The fork dug into the table and then bent due to the force—the force with which he slammed it.
Bang!

"What the hell are you even saying! You are crazy, Master! Family aren’t supposed to do things like that. Just keep quiet for now and eat the food. If you say something crazy like this again, I’m gonna walk out of the dining hall."

Seraphine wanted to answer him back, but she didn’t. He seemed to really be at his limit right now. His face was flushed red. She even noticed how he wasn’t looking at her, even for a moment now, not even glancing.
Just quietly eating while picking up a different fork.
It seemed she had to teach him the importance of family some other time. The way he didn’t deny they were already family was enough to make her heart feel warm.

But while the rest of the time was completely silent between them, she still couldn’t help but look at her adorable disciple while eating and tried to glance at his crotch too, to see if it was fine. Yet she wasn’t in luck, as her disciple’s seat was too far forward, right now. She couldn’t see anything.
Ten minutes had passed.
Both of them had finished their lunch.

Leon looked completely fine from the outside, and even the blush was completely gone—only a faint tint of red remained. But internally, his master’s words and what had happened previously swirled in his mind continuously, not giving him peace for a moment.

And the gorgeous beauty sitting across the table, looking at him with love on her face, didn’t make it any easier. He noticed her trying to glance at a certain part of him from time to time. It made his spine tingle a bit.
But he had understood an important thing about his master.
’The way Master regarded him as her family was quite different than how I had imagined.’

He didn’t mind how the relationship was going, but it weirded him out by the fact that he looked like a kid in front of her, so he couldn’t seem to take the step further right now. She was freaking 5 feet 11 inches (180 cm). He looked like a kid. He did know that in this world, sixteen is considered an adult.
The nobles would even arrange marriages between family members even at birth. The point is—she might see him as an adult. Or Master is just a pr—.
’No, it can’t be. Despite how cold she appears most of the time, she is very kind.’
He decided not to think about this right now and focus on what he was going to do.
"Master, are you okay now? Should I tell you about how I got strong so quickly?"
"Leon, Master has always been completely fine. Why are you asking me such a question?" A genuine look of confusion was on her face.
Seeing the look on her face, there was only one thought in his mind.
’Yep, Master, you’re definitely not okay.’
"Nothing. Should I continue?"
She hummed in response and nodded eagerly to his words like an excited child.

Leon couldn’t help but find her quite adorable right now. Sometimes she acted so cute and lovely, and sometimes completely crazy. He didn’t know how to define her. All he could say was his master was different—but he still loved her.
With a small smile on his face, instead of telling her verbally, from his inventory, he summoned the uncommon-ranked sword he had gotten after defeating the boss wolf monster.

Seraphine was shocked to see a sword suddenly appear in his hand out of nowhere. She couldn’t guess how he did it, and there was only one thing that came to her mind. The sword looked like a ranked weapon, too. She thought he might have gotten it inside the dungeon.
Now she understood how he had not a single monster mana core with him, even though she had told him especially not to miss a single one because of how rare they were.

She did know that he was the one who killed the boss, after hearing the words of the masked girl from a distance. Previously, she felt it was a pity that he had missed the core of the boss, too. But for her, coming out alive was already enough, so she didn’t mention those things to him.
’Had he leveled up? Is that why he had become so strong so fast?’
Still, she found it weird to feel a threat to that degree—even with that—as an increase in physical strength and having higher stats didn’t explain this massive improvement in him.

chapters.title: Chapter 63: Secrets no more
paragraphs: Seraphine decided to ask him directly instead of overthinking when he had planned to tell her this.
"Leon, storing things and taking them out of thin air—is that an ability of your class?"

She knew he had three different affinities, including space affinity, so his class might have abilities related to space. But it still didn’t make sense, as you were only supposed to get a class after completing the dungeon.
She remembered how she had to carry a large bag full of cores when she had first entered, so her earlier guess turned out to be invalid.
It didn’t make sense to her now. Only he could answer her, and she now thought she had underestimated the secret her disciple held.
Leon didn’t know how to explain it easily, so he told her in the way that seemed most appropriate to him.
"Master, it was a gift from a god."

Seraphine was shocked to her core. His words seemed too grand, and claiming it was a gift from a god felt surreal, yet his voice carried confidence, making it feel like he was fully certain, leaving no room for doubt.

She wasn’t unfamiliar with the term "god." There was a Church of the Goddess of Life and the Goddess of Light in almost every kingdom. They were said to be too powerful; no kingdom ever dared mess with them, as their roots extended even into the middle domain.
According to their beliefs, gods were said to be existences comparable to none—supreme beings meant to be worshipped by everyone. They could do anything; their power had no bounds.
She didn’t believe in such things as gods, but there were powerful organizations revolving around their existence. There had to be something to them to make it so.

"Leon, how are you so sure a god gave you this gift? I’ve read about something called bloodlines in ancient books. Some special people have them. They are said to grant special abilities and even enhance elemental affinity. It could be that you have some bloodline you just don’t know about."
"I don’t mind if you believe in any god, but calling your ability a gift from one seems a bit too far-fetched as an explanation."

Leon released a deep sigh. He had expected something like this, but he was patient. He didn’t want their relationship to be burned by this secret. He trusted her fully. He would share everything with her.

He couldn’t even imagine her betraying him for a second. She might do strange things sometimes and seem crazy too, but she could never harm him. So he believed. If his choice had consequences, he would bear them.
He wouldn’t let his cautious behavior ruin their relationship—the first time he felt truly loved and began to care about someone else, too.
Bringing his seat closer to her, he looked directly into her eyes, his tone more serious than ever.
"Master, I’m going to share everything about me with you, but be careful. If these things spread to others, I might really die because of it."
Just the existence of one of his treasures might start a kingdom-wide hunt for him. He was strong and confident in his abilities, but if an army came after him, he didn’t think he would survive.

Hearing what he had said made Seraphine’s expression harden. She was more serious than ever. She didn’t know what secrets he held, but if they could put his life at risk, she would never take them as a joke.

Leon started with the planet called Earth and how it had no magic. That was where he had previously lived as a boy. It was a bit hard to believe for Seraphine, but she completely trusted him and believed what he said was true.

Then he told her how he died at the age of sixteen due to the misfire of a powerful entity he didn’t understand. But calling it a god wasn’t too far-fetched, given how vast the entity appeared to him.

He mentioned he earned seven treasures from the entity as a gift and was later reborn in this world where she lived. The storage was just connected to his soul. He didn’t know how, but it was created by the same entity to store his treasures, and he found out he could store his own items in it, too.

Seraphine being shocked would be an understatement. Her mouth opened and closed a few times in disbelief after hearing what the treasure could do. She even felt like she shouldn’t be listening to this.
Hearing about the entity made her feel like a speck of dust. A being that could roam galaxies as if taking a walk, offering divine gifts like nothing, which could cause wars.
Even the most powerful and even the hermits would leave seclusion if they ever heard of such a thing. And all of this was destined for her, Leon. She knew he was special from the start—
—but she hadn’t known it was to a degree she couldn’t even fathom.

He mentioned how for seven years, he wasn’t aware of his memories of these things due to a condition. Born an orphan in the slums, he could have died early on, but he survived and met her only a few days after recovering his memories.

This explained everything to Seraphine now—why he seemed to have trained with a dagger for years. Even though he did train in his treasure for months, he clearly had natural talent, yet it still didn’t explain how he killed a level two goblin soldier with such a weak body of a seven-year-old without mana.
Normal people fighting for the first time would be too scared to even face such a monster.
And how, despite being only seven years old, he acted so cleverly with her. She didn’t think any normal sixteen-year-old could pull off a negotiation with a commander such as herself.
She praised him once again in her mind.
’My Leon is definitely special, with or without the treasures he has.’

chapters.title: Chapter 64: Secrets no more (2)
paragraphs: Leon paused for a moment and asked her one important question.
"Master, how do you feel after hearing all this?"
He hoped she didn’t change because of the things he had told her. It did seem he was some cliche chosen one, and she could even feel betrayed because of his identity.
He was holding his breath to hear her answer.

Seraphine noticed his nervousness. It seemed to her that he thought she would change because of it. She felt a bit annoyed to know this, as her love wasn’t so shallow—he should have been aware. But at the same time, she understood how big a thing it was for him. She was the first person he had shared these things with.
She felt quite happy to know this fact and forgave him for his lack of sense in her heart.

It doesn’t matter who he was before. He was her Leon, the boy she had picked up. The memories she had shared with him were all real. The boundless love she had felt for him was also real. Nothing can change these things for her.
And he even died at the tender age of 16. If he had been older, she would have felt a bit weird for a moment, but that was only it.
The family she had now—nothing can change that.
"Hmm, master felt nothing other than deep surprise because of how special my Leon is."
She did give a small hug afterward, while stopping herself from sniffing him and doing other things she wanted to do with him after the bite he had given to her.
It was just a nice, comfortable hug, which Leon appreciated quite a lot.
After the hug ended, Leon didn’t stop and continued.
He explained up to the point when it was time to get his class, which took longer than he had anticipated, only because of his master’s.

It was unexpected for him. Never would he have expected his master to cry. She started crying out of nowhere when he told her how he nearly died, and the only reason he survived was because of one of his treasures, which merged with him.

He had to be her emotional pillow for a whole fifteen minutes, her face buried in his chest. He comforted her by caressing her back for all 15 minutes, and repeated many times that he was fine and wasn’t going to leave her—she didn’t have to cry now.

At the end, only with a promise that he would never leave her, she did stop crying. Kaela did tell him master was more vulnerable than he had seen. He saw it firsthand now. He promised to never make her cry. She was the one who was crying, but he also felt the pain in his heart because of it.

After she had stopped crying, she was quite docile. Her eyes and nose were a bit red. Despite that fact, she looked stunning as ever, or it even enhanced a bit of her charm with her flowing purple hair, her amethyst eyes, with her beautiful face.
It made him want to just protect the poor thing, but he knew, despite how she looked, she was very strong.
"Master, my actual class rank is not A rank but instead SSS rank."
She tilted her head cutely in her confusion to his explanation of rank, as she had never heard of such a thing. So he had to explain to her what ranks come after the A rank and the SSS rank.

He can even see that there wasn’t even a look of shock on her face now. It seems to him she was getting used to it. She didn’t seem to have any desire to know more than what he had told her. After his explanation of everything, she didn’t ask anything from him anything.
Well, he told her everything, which could be the reason she didn’t ask anything.
Her behavior had also returned to normal.

"So Leon, your stats are even higher than mine, only at level 6 because of your class rank, and you have an absurd amount of mana because of the orb you merged with. And not even that—you have affinity to all the elements in the world, which you aren’t even aware of how many there are in total."
’My disciple is a monster living in human skin.’

She knew it wouldn’t be long before he would surpass her quite easily. Right now seemed the perfect opportunity to fight him as an equal, which was why tomorrow would be when they would have a fight, not just a sparring match like they used to.
Leon only nodded in response to her words.
"Master, do you want to come to my room so we can try to go to my dimension, which I mentioned, where time was 1000 times faster than outside? We can train together there."

"I will join you, but not today—tomorrow after we have a fight as equals."
She had seen a hint of hesitation on his face for a moment. She didn’t like that one bit.

"Hmph! Don’t underestimate your master just because you have so much mana and your stats are a bit higher than mine. Master has a secret weapon of her own, and I am much more experienced than you. I would be able to handle you for now."
"Just worry about yourself, my cute disciple. You will lose if you let your guard down. Master was going to go all out tomorrow."

Leon only hesitated because he believed that if they fought, this mansion would be destroyed. He loved living in such a luxurious place, and more importantly, he didn’t want any of them to get injured. So his determination to learn the life element increased even more.
"You are talking about your Lightning Aura, master, aren’t you?"
Seraphine was shocked this time, when she had thought he was getting used to it.

It did seem he was some cliche chosen one, and she could even feel betrayed because of his identity.
He was holding his breath to hear her answer.
Seraphine noticed his nervousness.
It seemed to her that he thought she would change because of it.
She felt a bit annoyed to know this, as her love wasn’t so shallow—he should have been aware.
But at the same time, she understood how big a thing it was for him.
