"Leon, are you just gonna run like this... or actually try to attack me?"

Leon looked at his master with a pale, deadpan expression. If his face could speak, it would clearly say,Are you serious?He knew exactly what she was trying—baiting him in close for one final, decisive blow.
But the setup was too cliché. He wasn’t going to fall for it.
"No. I’m not going to," he replied flatly.
Seraphine had already expected him to reject her taunt. So, there was only one thing left to do now.

"There’s no point in continuing this, my dear disciple," she said, voice calm but tinged with defeat. "All my mana will be gone in one more minute. I can’t even touch you. You’ve basically won. You can bombard me endlessly with your magic... I don’t even know how long I could endure."
She slowly sheathed her sword back into the scabbard at her waist.
"Let’s go on our date now. It seems Master lost today."
Leon also began sheathing his blade, but mid-motion, her figurevanished—and in the next breath, she appeared right in front of him, fist cocked for a devastating blow in her final form.
FWOOOM—!
Leon didn’t move. He stood perfectly still.
Seraphine froze—literally. Her fist halted inches from his face. No matter how hard she struggled, she couldn’t move an inch.

He had been ready. He’d usedSpatial Freeze, fueled by two hundred mana, without hesitation. With his reverse-mana pool and spatial awareness, he could predict exactly when she’d strike—especially with how head-on the move was. He didn’t take chances.
She was locked in place. Not even her aura could help her now.
It had only been a second, but she understood clearly—this was enough. The fight was over. She couldn’t move. She couldn’t resist. And he hadn’t even broken a sweat.
’So this is the power of the space element...’she thought.

It all made sense now—his ability to teleport, to dodge every one of her blows despite not matching her in raw strength. She knew it was broken from the start. But experiencing it firsthand was something else entirely.
Leon stepped forward and came face to face with her, his eyes meeting hers.
Without a word, he leaned in and kissed her.
Even then, he didn’t release the freeze.
"Master, you’re so cute—trying to make me lower my guard. I didn’t know you played tricks like that," Leon said with a teasing smile.

Seraphine felt a flush of shame. This was supposed to be alessonfor him—one where, after winning, she could proudly remind him never to show his back to an opponent. But it seemed her clever disciple never gave her that chance to begin with.
He whispered, "Master, let’s go now. There’s no point continuing. Let’s just have our date."
And with a small smile, he added, "Also... you really need to teach me all your techniques. I had no way to fight you head-on."

He could have unleashed powerful attacks—like the condensed lightning spear, a slightly weaker version of the one that destroyed a mountain. But those were too dangerous. He didn’t dare use them, not when her safety was at risk.

Truthfully, Leon knew he could’ve ended this much faster, even without that. His regular attacks could have been made much stronger and far more relentless. But he held back, intentionally keeping their power just low enough for her to dodge in time. With ten to twelve times her mana reserve, he was practically invisible in this battle.
And the reason was simple.
Even though he had warned her he would heal her if anything went wrong—he had never intended to hurt her in the first place.
Seraphine slowly released her aura, her techniques, her skills—undoing everything. Seeing that, Leon finally lifted the space freeze.
She looked at him quietly and said, "You didn’t give it your all, did you?"
He didn’t respond right away. But seeing no point in denying it, he gave a small nod.
He had done her wrong. She’d wanted a real fight.
But how could he explain? In a real battle, against a deadly enemy, he wouldn’t have hesitated. He would’ve frozen space and ended it in one move.
"Why didn’t you even attack me properly?" she pressed. "And don’t say those onslaughts of elemental spells—they conveniently gave me half a second to dodge. You did that on purpose, didn’t you?"
"If the attacks had been just a little faster... a little stronger... I would’ve been done for. Leon, answer me. Could you have done it?"
Leon met her eyes. This time, he answered clearly.
"Yes."
She nodded.
’As expected. Ten times my mana... and such control over multiple elements... I knew I would lose.’

She looked quite stern—but in the next moment, her entire demeanor of interrogation and toughness melted away completely. She hugged his body tightly, wrapping her arms around his head as his face pressed against her soft breasts.
"I knew my Leon was very strong," she giggled softly, "but this Master was really surprised. Hehe... don’t worry, Master will teach you every single one of her techniques."
Leon hummed in response, still face-buried in her warmth. He felt genuinely relaxed. She didn’t take the fight harshly—even after losing, she just played it off like it was a routine Tuesday task.
But then her tone shifted.
She gently lifted his face, holding his cheeks as her eyes searched his—deep, radiant, and full of something more.
"But my disciple..." her voice softened. "Master is still upset. I wasn’t even able to see how strong my Leon really is."

She had already lost completely the day she realized she couldn’t live without him. This match was nothing compared to that. But still, as a teacher, shewantedto witness it—to see the true depth of his strength. It made her proud just thinking about it.
Leon didn’t panic. Instead, he calmly turned his head toward the deep crater in the distance—nearly a hundred meters away—surrounded by massive rubble and shattered earth.

She blinked, following his gaze.
"With my strongest attack... I destroyed it in one blow."

She stared at the devastation. The rubble wasn’t just scattered—it was obliterated. The crater alone looked like a wound carved into the earth by nature’s wrath itself. A natural disaster wouldn’t have looked out of place there.
His tone shifted slightly, growing more serious.
"I can create a slightly weaker version of that same attack... about fifty percent of its strength... even while dodging your strikes."
He didn’t finish. He let the unspoken truth settle between them.
Seraphine imagined it clearly. That kind of attack—onherduring battle? There wouldn’t have been anything left. Not a trace.
Only now, after seeing it firsthand, did she truly realize...
Just how terrifying a monster her beloved disciple really was.

chapters.title: Chapter 79: The Date
paragraphs: Leon and Seraphine decided to leave the dimension shortly after the dull fight ended. Leon couldn’t bring himself to actually harm her, even knowing he could heal her back afterward.
But Seraphine didn’t mind. She had seen how capable he was, and that was enough for her. The devastation shown to her caused by his strongest attack still left her shaken.
Even at half strength, that attack could have killed hundreds in a single strike—regardless of whether they were as strong as her or just random nobodies.

Somewhere unknown, the mysterious lady who had been watching the fight felt deeply dissatisfied with how it ended. She was admittedly impressed by Leon’s control over space in such a short period, but it was obvious he never intended to hurt the woman from the start. That made the entire battle boring for her.
She had been excited—expecting the fight to end in typical human fashion. Perhaps the woman would reward him for winning, something lewd and dramatic. But no. They just left right afterward.
She was disappointed in her master.
"Leon, let me go back and change. You should change your clothes too—we’ll meet in the hallway that leads to the mansion’s exit."
"Okay. Come back quickly," he replied.

Leon stood at the right of the mansion gate, dressed in a fitted white high-collared shirt with faint silver embroidery that caught the light when he moved. The tailored fabric traced the lines of his frame with quiet precision, and the loose sleeves added a touch of elegance. His long silver hair fell neatly around his shoulders, and under the soft light, his sharp features and calm expression gave him an almost statuesque presence—striking, composed, and impossible to ignore.
He waited for Seraphine to return. Ten minutes had passed, and she still wasn’t back.
He hadn’t known his master could ever be this late.
Then he saw her.
Her figure appeared in the distance, and for a moment, Leon froze.

Seraphine walked toward him with slow, graceful steps, dressed in a striking black dress that clung to her curves like midnight silk. The corset hugged her waist tightly, accentuating her figure, while lace-trimmed gloves and a jeweled choker added a gothic allure. Her long lavender hair cascaded freely behind her, catching the soft light as she moved. The deep slit in her dress revealed glimpses of her pale thighs—each step, a quiet temptation. Her amethyst eyes stayed locked on him, half-lidded and unreadable—but undeniably focused.
’Wow master look so beautiful’
He had never seen his master in such a feminine dress in the past three years. But he had to admit—she looked absolutely gorgeous in it.
Seraphine stopped in front of him. Her voice was calm, but inside, she was surprisingly nervous.
"How is it, Leon?"
He should’ve complimented her immediately. But as she stepped closer, even more radiant up close, he found himself briefly lost in her presence.
"Seraphine, you look gorgeous. You should wear dresses like this more often."
He had decided to not call her master for the day as they going to be couples today.
She giggled softly in response and wrapped her arm around his, leading him toward the carriage waiting outside.
"Hehe, if my Leon likes it... then I’ll wear these kinds of dresses more often—especially for you."
As they exited the mansion, she led him to the carriage. Everyone who looked their way—even Kaela, who was in charge of the transport—paused in surprise at the commander’s appearance.

The market of Duskmoor buzzed with life. Lanterns floated above cobbled streets, casting warm glows that danced across merchant stalls and crystal shop windows. The scent of roasted nuts, sweet mana confections, and enchanted herbs hung in the air.
Amid the noise and motion, they stood out like a tale come to life.

Seraphine, the cold and untouchable Commander of Duskmoor, walked beside a silver-haired young man—taller than her, his expression calm, his presence quietly commanding. Her arm was linked with his, dress flowing like woven starlight. He wore clean white, understated but regal.
People whispered. The Commander... was on a date.
But Seraphine didn’t glance at them. She smiled, leading Leon through the heart of the city like the crowd didn’t exist.
She stopped at a small dessert stall known for its enchanted duskblossom sweets, holding up two fingers. "Two of those," she said.
Then she turned to Leon, soft-eyed. "They melt if you don’t eat them quickly. Want me to feed you?"
Leon blinked, amused. "I don’t mind, Seraphine—but would you really do that in public?"
He can see there were lot of eyes on them.
Without a word, she picked one up between her gloved fingers, leaned in, and placed it against his lips.
"Eat," she whispered.
He did. The sweetness burst across his tongue with a cool, floral chill. He wasn’t sure what stunned him more—the flavor or the way she looked at him while he tasted it.
Later, they walked hand-in-hand through a glasswork lane where enchanted chimes hung from floating rods between buildings. Each one played a faint melody as they passed beneath.
Seraphine stopped at a music crystal vendor and lifted a tiny orb to Leon’s ear. It played a soft, warm tune—gentle notes like falling petals.
"I used to listen to this when I couldn’t sleep," she murmured.
Leon looked at her. "You still don’t sleep easily?"
"Not unless my disciple lets me hug him during the day."
He said nothing, but gently squeezed her hand.

They stopped by a street artist sketching couples with swift, practiced strokes. Seraphine paid him before Leon could protest and sat beside him on a low stone bench, resting her head on his shoulder.
"You’re enjoying this too much," Leon said, voice low.
"I’m allowed to," she replied, not moving. "You’re mine for the day."

As night fell and the lanterns above shimmered brighter, they reached a bridge overlooking Duskmoor’s glowing river. The water glowed faintly from alchemical channels beneath its surface, casting luminous ripples in the dark.
Seraphine leaned forward on the railing, watching their reflections shift on the water’s surface.
Leon stepped behind her, arms gently circling her waist.
"This is... the first time I’ve seen you like this," he whispered against her ear.
It was true. She often clung to him in passing—used him like a pillow, teased him in private—but this... this was different.
This was Seraphine free.
No rank. No pressure. Just a woman who wanted to be seen, to be held.
She leaned back into him, smiling.
"Then you should make sure you remember it."

Seraphine’s eyes locked as an even more intense swirl appeared in her eyes. His words, his slight obsession with her, the anger he felt for her, and even wanting to mention killing them outright.
The love that started to become just like hers.
The anger that could burn everything for her.
It made her feel euphoric all over her body. She even got wet.
A wide smile spread across her beautiful face as she answered him.
"I love you so, so much, Leon. I knew you would be upset, which is why the master had prepared something special for you."
A slight pause. Her voice sounded again with a grin on her beautiful face.
"Tomorrow we are gonna depart for the Kingdom of Shampain. There is..."

sentences.text: "Hehe, as expected, my Leon noticed it too.
I knew it, but first, why are you calling me master even now...
You can call me by my name, like yesterday.
I’d love it when you say my name."
"I thought you liked it when I called you master.
If you really want me to stop calling—"
She stopped him midway.
"It’s alright.
You can also call me master from time to time, as usual.
I like the sound of it as much as you calling me by name."
"Hmph!
So don’t you dare think you can stop calling me master, no matter how strong you become," her voice sounded serious as she was telling him some law that shouldn’t be broken.
’My master and her hopeless fetishes.’
Leon didn’t mind it, so he agreed to her as he knew from the start that she wouldn’t want him to stop calling her master.
Her slip-up earlier had made her realize her desire, so she corrected herself.
"Alright, alright!
You don’t have to be so serious about this, especially when I am asking about the people who were following us during our date."
"Don’t you realize, my hopeless master, which is more important?"
"Of course, my dear Leon, calling me master is more important.
I have my priorities straight, and you think I am hopeless?
When we are alone at night, I would tax you for hurting my feelings," with a deadpan look, Seraphine replied, and at the end, lust was clearly visible on her face.
"Okay, whatever you want.
You are going to pass out anyway, so now just tell me who those people were."
Seraphine couldn’t help but blush slightly, but she didn’t look at all like a shy girl.
Instead, her eyes were locked into his, as she had made a mental note to make him eat those words.
To do that, she would do the same to him, giving him pleasure so high that he could pass out from exhaustion.
’Just you wait for the night, disciple.
Master going to teach your big thick monster a lesson it won’t forget.’
But who was going to tell her the feat she was trying to achieve was almost impossible for an anomaly like Leon, who had even shocked an ancient being by beating his meat continuously for a day?
Her tone didn’t even change to a serious one as she said in a casual note.

"A few are the people sent by the Duke’s eldest son of the neighboring kingdom, the Kingdom of Shampain, who thinks he can own me, saying he will take me as his first wife, even announcing it to the world as if my opinion doesn’t even matter in this regard.
He thinks no one can stop him because their kingdom is the strongest.
He is most likely waiting for the right moment..."
After a whole 15 minutes of details.
She had finally finished.
There was no trace of emotion other than disgust on her face when she told him everything.
The only reason these people didn’t directly make a move was that she was too strong for them to handle.
But finding her weakness was a different matter—something they could take advantage of.
Now he finally understood why he was never allowed to travel outside without her accompanying him during his past 3 years.

He had just misunderstood her, but knowing about this even now made him feel her warmth once again—the care and love she had shown for the last 3 years, even when he wasn’t appreciative of her at first.
Her love was loud, unwavering, and unconditional—a devotion that endures even in the absence of his denial.
But now he would make sure she would be happier than ever with him as his woman.
His eyes turned to glint as even his aura began to leak out for the first time, as never had he ever felt this much anger in his life.
’The Duke’s son of the strong kingdom on the lower domain, their own kingdom’s youngest prince.’
These were the two who caused his anger the most, especially the Duke’s eldest son, who had the guts to announce his Seraphine as his future wife in front of countless many.
The youngest prince didn’t have much power, but he also had eyes on his Seraphine, wanting her to join his harem.

Caused by the chain reaction of these two highly influential people, the crown prince of the Kingdom of Shampain also had his eyes on her for a different reason—to gain the support of the Duke’s eldest son, who was likely gonna take over the dukedom.

And lastly.

One of the wealthiest merchants of the lower domain who wanted her to be the face of his products and had been pestering her for months because of her popularity all over the lower kingdom, not just because she was one of the strongest women in the lower domain, but because of the high-ranking individuals she attracted naturally.
’Do they think my Seraphine is a pawn or object they could control...
I really want to erase all of them from existence.’
He could imagine why Seraphine couldn’t do anything despite having the power to crush these pests individually.

"I really want to kill them." His eyes, which had a slight swirl in them, looked into her violet eyes.
He knew his reaction was a bit intense, but it was his real feeling.
For the first time in both his lives, he had found something so precious and warm that he could never give up on.
And some people wanted to take that away from him, treating her as a toy.
Never.
Their death would be the least of their worries once he met them.

I knew you would be upset, which is why the master had prepared something special for you."

Her voice sounded again with a grin on her beautiful face.
"Tomorrow we are gonna depart for the Kingdom of Shampain.
There is..."

chapters.title: Chapter 85: An Assasination or Eradication
paragraphs: "Tomorrow we are gonna depart for the Kingdom of Shampain."

Excitement filled Leon’s eyes as he heard what she said. Kingdom of Shampain—they should be ready for what chaos he was gonna bring there, but he didn’t interrupt as she seemed to have much to tell him.

"There is, as there always had been, every year a grand event organized by the Ascendant Academy to display the prowess of their students to the rest of the world." She paused for a moment as she continued while completely focusing on his expression because she knew he was gonna like this part. "Ascendant Academy was not originally made by the Shampain kingdom. From what I know, most of the staff and headmaster are from the middle domain, or could be even higher, as you have broadened my horizon about this world the other day."
"The academy was also the reason that the Shampain kingdom had become the most powerful kingdom over the years, just because it is located in their capital city of Hemsburg."
"It is also the academy where I had attended for 4 years when I was much younger. They are mysterious and powerful—no one can mess with them."
A grin appeared on her face as she continued the next part.

"We were only going there at first because, when I learned you had an affinity for all the elements but didn’t have proper knowledge and ideas about how they would work, I had thought it would be a great experience for you to witness the festival firsthand."

Leon was listening quietly to everything she was telling him and seriously thought this was a big opportunity for him to see people with different affinities fighting each other. He would have massive growth in understanding his own elements.
But there was one question in his mind. He asked her as the grin on her face told him she hadn’t told him everything.
"Would the Duke’s eldest son also be participating in the event? Is he also enrolled in the academy?"

"Hehe, my dear disciple, you have guessed correctly. While my intention when attending the festival with you was different at first, luckily, he is also a fourth-year student in the academy. The festival and the battles happening in them were not just for show—many students even lost their lives in them. Your results would decide whether you would graduate from the academy or not. Getting a graduation degree from Ascendant is like proving your worth to the world and spreading your name far and wide, other than the golden life which was guaranteed afterward."
"Good, but would I be able to participate in the event? I am not a student of the academy."
Seraphine said while another thought crossed her mind.
"No, you can’t participate since you are not a student of the academy."

Leon gave her a look. She told him everything, raising his expectations and mentioning that the bastard would be there too, only to say he can’t participate in the event and would miss out on the chance to kill him without much unnecessary drama that can come along with his status.
He thought for a moment. He was calm now.
"It doesn’t matter either way, master. His being just present was enough for me. I don’t need the festival to deal with him."
’Oh! My disciple is going rogue for me—how cute! My Leon is the best!’
She decided to play with him a little, as for the full surprise she would give once they reached the academy.
"But my disciple, if you did as little as to draw his blood, the whole kingdom of Shampain would be your enemy. I don’t think my cute disciple can handle an army in his current state."
Leon smirked and replied to her.

"Don’t worry, master. I am not stupid—nobody would know how he disappeared. I am confident I can pull this off, so if the culprit is not even found, who are they gonna attack with their army? I would make sure he dies in the academy. It would be more fun this way—mysterious Ascendant Academy vs Strongest kingdom. It would be interesting, wouldn’t it?"

Seraphine was a bit surprised by how sly her disciple was. She had expected to hear him say something about killing him without anyone finding out, but turning the academy against the kingdom—that would create a war.
Her spine tingled because of the rush of excitement she was feeling, and she also wholeheartedly believed he could pull this off with his overpowered space element and other elements.
’Should I just not tell him I have a way to let him take part in the event?’
Seraphine was seriously thinking whether she should let him do what he wanted.
For now, she had no answer—she would think about this in her free time. It would be more of thinking to get the answer.

For now, she had to enjoy this lovely moment where her Leon was thinking of starting wars for her. She couldn’t wait for the night when she would let him know how touched she felt by his passionate love for her.
Her hand traced his face gently.
"My dear Leon had gone rogue, but the master likes it very much."

After finishing eating, they continued talking for much longer, as Leon wanted to know everything about the kingdom of Shampain, the academy, and the festival taking place, since he had to go through with his plan.
While getting information from her master, who was clearly enjoying himself whenever he would ask another question.

At the end, he had learned so much more about everything, and even the fact that the master was at the top of her academy festival 5 years ago, which meant there were at least nine more people as strong as Seraphine in the public’s eyes. As for the rest, there must be more, but he wasn’t aware of them.

He did ask her what she would rank herself among those 10 powerful people, but she said she was clueless as she wasn’t much in contact with them, but she did say she would definitely be in the top 5 strongest people on the lower domain, not just those 10.
The strongest people of the lower domain, they were talking about, and knowing his master was so well-renowned made him feel proud of her.
He learned it would take 7-10 days’ worth of journey to reach the capital city of Shampain.

Which meant for him, 19 to 27 years in the dimensional space. He was gonna train like never before, and once he reached the capital, he would make sure his name would bring terror to the whole of the kingdom of Shampain.

He did say to Seraphine he would hide his identity, but that’s only if he didn’t have the power to face their so-called army. He would very much like their kingdom to know about his terror if possible, just like that bastard Duke’s son had announced Seraphine would be his wife, without giving any regard to her, and pestering her for years.
’I wonder if it would be a silent assassination or eradication of an army.’
’It seems Life steal would have a chance to shine much sooner than I anticipated.’

chapters.title: Chapter 86: Seraphine Plans [Bonus]
paragraphs: After the late breakfast.
Inside Leon’s room.

Leon and Seraphine are standing face to face with each other. In Leon’s right hand, the Dimensional Hourglass was displaying its mysterious nature by floating on his hand, with black sand inside moving sideways, defying gravity.
Sending a message: Gravity is for the weak.

"Master, I want to try something. While we can go train inside the Time Dimension by entering it physically, that won’t stop us from aging. It had its own perks of being the ability to comprehend elements much faster for me, yet the factor of not aging while getting slower progress was still much more appealing."
"Otherwise, during the time we would travel to the capital city of Shampain Kingdom, Hemsburg, we would become old."

Seraphine gives him a nod, as it would make them 17 to 19 years older. They are human, even when reaching the level 10 apprentice rank. The most we can live is 200 at most, so nearly 20 years would be one-tenth of their lifespan.
"So you are telling me that I would also be able to enter the dimension space in conscious form like you?" she inquired.

"Yes, you should be. The last time I entered it in physical form with you, I had a feeling that if I allowed it, you would be able to do the same as me and enter it using your consciousness only, and not age at all while training for years."

Seraphine’s heart beats frantically just by the sound of it. It would be like a dream come true for her, having so much time to train while not worrying about dying of old age without ever advancing in your strength.

The reason why she took such drastic measures 5 years ago, entering the forbidden mist, was that she didn’t want her journey to end in this small place when there is a much wider place out there named the middle domain.

People of the middle domain have longer life spans than the lower domain, and have the power to act as a king in the lower domain. While she had no desire to settle in a small bubble, it was the truth nonetheless.
"Show me your hand," Leon asked.
Seraphine did as she was told, but nervousness was quite visible on her face as this would likely be a life-changing event for her and even determine whether the gap between them would increase.
She was not the one who wanted to live like a burden to him, but like his proud woman who pulls her own weight, while she does have the desire to be spoiled from time to time.
But being a burden, her pride wouldn’t allow it, and she knew she had the potential to even reach a lesser divine, like he had told her earlier.
She wanted to reach that realm of power, the lesser divine, where one doesn’t have to worry about aging at all, an immortal existence.
A life together with her Leon forever was her motivation now, not just stop at this small world of Velaria, and to go much, much further than just the so-called middle domain.
He did notice the anxiousness on her face, but didn’t say anything as he was 90% sure it would work. Without trying, he can’t give her false hope.

Holding her hand, he imagined giving her permission to enter the conscious world of the dimensional hourglass. Right after that, a tattoo of an hourglass replicating the one Leon was holding appeared on Seraphine’s hand, and disappeared right after as if merging with her skin, leaving no trace of it on her spotless skin.
Leon doesn’t have to say anything now. He felt the crushing yet warm hug from his master on his body.
"Leon! I can feel it. With just a thought, I can enter the time dimension like before with only my consciousness."

Her excitement was justified, as this ability was too broken. The connection she felt was through the soul. She felt she could enter the world from anywhere in the world, but she also felt that without his permission, it was impossible to enter, and his thought alone would be enough to kick her out.

Which she wasn’t worried about in the least, but in her mind, countless new possibilities arose. She still hadn’t told him about her ideas of building their empire inside the dimensional space, and this ability of the dimension treasure gave her confidence to a new, profound level.

They didn’t have to show it to them. For the most trusted people and for hiring strong individuals who wanted to move forward, this would be something they would risk their lives to get a chance to spend even a day inside the time dimension.
"Leon, do you feel you can give access to people without taking out the treasure?"
Hearing her question, he felt confused as he didn’t think anyone other than Seraphine would allow anyone to enter his time dimension.
But he still gave her a nod as he could use it while his treasure was in his inventory. So he was confident in his ability to give access to the dimension without actually taking it out.
"Why do you ask that, master?"

Seraphine only giggled hearing his question, as she wasn’t gonna reveal her plan to him before she makes a much more thorough plan, a plan so foolproof that even her cautious Leon wouldn’t be able to reject it.
’Our empire will be built soon.’

She doesn’t think it would take much time because of the ability of the overpowered treasure itself. The empires that took thousands of years to establish their foundation would take them a mere year. It was too big an opportunity she couldn’t miss.
Leon put the treasure back in his inventory. There is still so much time before they depart for the kingdom of Shampain tomorrow. They have to train.
Sitting cross-legged face to face with each other.
"Master, just think about entering the dimension. It would work, and you have to teach me all your techniques."
While he can’t learn skills without the skill stone, techniques could be passed down to one another through teaching.

"Of course, my dear disciple. If the master doesn’t teach you my own technique, how can I call myself your master? I will teach you everything. We have a lot of time. You should be easily able to learn all my techniques to at least a novice level at the very least before leaving tomorrow."
She gave him a light kiss on his lips as she then tried to enter the dimension with her mind sitting in her previous position.
Leon felt that someone was trying to enter the dimension, and he gave his permission with his mind. Now seeing Seraphine’s eyes closed, lost in her world, he knew she was inside.
And he followed right afterward.
"What took you so long? Are you doing something naughty with your master’s body when she was not aware?"
"Master, have you forgotten where we are currently? I have entered the dimension a second after you."
Now it finally clicked in her mind as to why, for the past 16 minutes, she had to wait for him, because it was only 1 second outside.
’This treasure truly is godly,’ she couldn’t help but realize it once again.

chapters.title: Chapter 92: Master Imparting a Valuable Lesson
paragraphs: Hearing his words, Seraphine was confused too, as even when she hadn’t fought the terror of a monster inside the forbidden mist, her techniques’ ranks weren’t even adept rank, and mana enhancement was the only adept rank technique she had.
She still had the feeling that she was reaching closer to an unknown power she couldn’t fully grasp, but from Leon’s words, he seemed completely clueless, which made Seraphine feel very strange.
"That’s strange. You should have the feeling of reaching an unknown power, like how I felt before grasping the lightning Aura."
Leon nodded to her words, as that was indeed very weird. He was exceptional at everything, yet he had yet to feel the slightest bit of feeling for reaching Aura, as if it didn’t even exist to him.

But Seraphine wasn’t the one to just leave this topic like this. She had to get to the bottom of why her genius disciple was struggling so much with Aura. She would have been on the verge of achieving level 1 Aura right now.

She did know that she had gained her Aura in a life-or-death battle, in desperate need, but even if that hadn’t happened, in a few years, she would have achieved the unknown power called Aura either way.

"Don’t worry, Leon. Your master will get to the bottom of this and find the actual problem, so you should tell me everything since you started learning elements for the first time until now. Explain every single detail to me."
They had all the time in the world inside this space. She didn’t mind if she had to listen to his story for a day or even a week.

Finishing the bath, they were now sitting on luxurious wooden chairs with a circular table in between. On one end sat Seraphine, on the other Leon. Both of them had serious expressions on their faces.

Seraphine had stored a lot of different things in her Leon’s inventory, since the time she knew he could use those things here, even in his conscious form, and the chairs and table were only one of those things.
For 12 hours straight, Leon explained to her which element he had started and how he learned it, and what the thought behind it was.

Only after 6 hours of his explanation, Seraphine had completely pointed out what was the big mistake he was making, which was holding him back. She also felt surprised, even with such a false mindset, he was able to achieve such results. She now realized how terrifying a rank 7 affinity actually was.
If he had the right mindset, he would have at least twice or even thrice as much growth by now. He could even have already had Aura in not one but multiple elements.

She felt good, she had this discussion with him, as even after the 6-hour point, she didn’t stop him, as his methods were quite insightful to her. It was giving her so many ideas and also broadening her horizons.
The training after this would be much more fruitful for her, not just for Leon. She knew it.
Seeing the confident smug on her master’s face, Leon knew she had pointed out what the problem was.
He didn’t ask her as her voice sounded.
"How can you be so smart and dumb at the same time, my disciple?"
Leon didn’t know whether to feel good or bad, but he didn’t interrupt as she continued.

The smugness on her face didn’t go away for a moment as Seraphine felt like a real master who was imparting a valuable lesson to her disciple for the first time, which would give him massive growth, if the lesson itself was the very basic foundation of all magic.
For 30 whole minutes, Seraphine had the smug look on her face, which Leon only found cute at this point, as she was really enjoying all of this.

The more he listened to her, the more it sounded stupid at the same time true, and his way of thinking. He knew the truth of the element to some degree because his scientific knowledge seemed almost illogical and stupid.
After giving her explanation, which changed his whole point of view about elements, she asked one question to let him see how stupid his logic was.

"Disciple, let us assume for a moment that the nonsense you spoke—drawn from your former world’s understanding of lightning—holds some truth. That is the essence of the element, defined by science and form. Then tell me this: if your so-called truth is absolute, why can I summon the same lightning with a mere thread of mana, without knowing a single thing about the complex principles you spoke of?"
Leon had no answer to that, and realized how against his thinking was to the core of the world of magic and mana.

"Mana and the elements are profound. They aren’t things you can define so easily. Thinking you’ve understood them with just scraps of knowledge—that’s not understanding. That’s just arrogant and plain stupid."
"Your mindset must reach toward the unknown. Do not be shackled by the shallow certainty of your past—it’s a weight that stifles growth."
"Treat mana and the elements as limitless. You are treading into the unknown, and that... must be your starting point."
"The only reason you have reached such a level of control on elements with that mindset was due to your overwhelming talent and your experimenting with elements, which boosted your growth."
Leon looked deep into her eyes and said.
"Thank you, master."

After hearing her words and realizing how wrong his approach had been, he felt free, and he had now thrown off those logical reasons of the previous world that were just binding him. He could use them to fuel his curiosity and get different ideas, but in this world of magic, that scientific knowledge might just be a speck of dust in this universe where godly beings reside.

Seraphine, hearing his words, just waved her hand as that was her duty as his master and family, but it felt nice that she was able to give this basic yet fundamental knowledge. She knew once they reached the Hemsburg, her Leon would be even more terrifying than she had anticipated.
As this small yet fundamental change in his point of view was going to make his training many times more effective.

chapters.title: Chapter 93: Aura
paragraphs: After the change in his fundamental beliefs about mana and elements—or rather, the whole magical world—slowly but surely, the rate at which his control over the elements increased.
Not instantly, but he saw only little changes over time, which made his belief even stronger over the past year.

Realizing what was correct and fully believing in that fact—leaving behind his previous beliefs—was a different matter, and it took a year to fully change his core understanding of mana, elements, and magic, which made the speed of learning elements many times faster.

And the feeling of an unknown power drawing closer as he made progress in the elements was getting stronger and stronger, especially in his lightning element, which he had the most control over among all the elements. He knew the unknown power was the concept of elements, the first level of which was Aura, which he was about to reach in the lightning element.
That wasn’t all, as over the last year, he had focused on practicing his Rajin’s Descent, hoping to bring it to the Grandmaster level, and it felt like he would reach that level in a few weeks.
His control over the lightning element was now three times stronger than before, compared to the other elements.
He could reach the limit of controlling 1,000 mana in the lightning element, but he had never truly launched an attack with it; he had only created a huge, towering spear and canceled it right after.

But this was now his strongest attack, and the devastation it would cause would be many times stronger than the one he used to destroy the small mountain. That wasn’t all. With all the other elements, using 700 mana at the same time was now possible.
The only reason he couldn’t reach 1,000—same as the lightning element—was due to his control over those elements, not because of mental pressure.

Another two months had passed. Leon was standing in front of a large mountain, using the Rajin’s Descent technique. The horn made of lightning was pulsating with intense energy as he punched the gigantic mountain, 200 meters tall, in front of which he looked like an ant.
Every punch made the ground beneath him tremble with the shock. Small craters, five meters wide and one meter deep, were being imprinted on the surface with each punch.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
More
He continued, pouring every ounce of his power into every attack while completely focused on maintaining the circulation of the lightning element within his body.

Suddenly, the horn on top of his head burst into lightning particles and entered his body. His eyes gleamed with excitement as he saw the message floating in front of him. He ignored it completely and continued punching.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Now, instead of the horn, only faint lightning crackled all over his body—thin as threads of silk—but the color of the lightning was no longer glowing yellow; it had reached a hue closer to gold.
Another punch.

The devastation it caused was many times stronger than before. Instead of five-meter craters, the surface was now marked with ones closer to twenty meters wide and three meters deep. The tremors it caused to the surrounding area were even greater. Small rocks shook and floated in the air with every punch.
Seraphine, from a distance of fifty meters, could clearly hear the loud booming sound. She realized that he had reached the Grandmaster level in Rajin’s Descent.
She had thought it would take him at least two years to achieve that, but the growth he had experienced from a single fundamental realization was far more than she had imagined.

And she knew reaching Grandmaster in another technique would take even less time, as he had told her two months ago that he had completely overcome his beliefs from the previous world, and there was nothing holding him back anymore.
So these past one year and two months were not uniform—his speed had only reached its peak in the last two months.

Seraphine had just achieved Master rank in the Skybreaker Draw technique two days ago, and now she was aiming to reach Grandmaster level in her Mana Body Enhancement. She knew it would take years to achieve this.

She just hoped that by the time her six-year period was over—which meant eighteen years for Leon—she would have reached the Grandmaster level of mastery. It would definitely make her twice, or even thrice, as strong. It was the most fundamental technique that required no skill scroll to learn, as it would automatically appear in your system once you learned to control mana.

People called it a gift of the system. She believed it was the best choice for her to train this, as it would also improve her mana control, allowing her to spend less mana on her techniques and skills. She didn’t think she needed to advise her disciple, as with the rate of his progress, he had so much time that he would definitely attain Grandmaster level in Mana Body Enhancement, too.

She was excited for the day they would reach the Kingdom of Champagne. She even felt now that her disciple might actually take on an army by the time they reached there, as his strength was increasing at a terrifying pace.
Her shock didn’t end there. Suddenly, she felt a familiar energy coming from the direction where Leon was training. She recognized it immediately.
Aura.
She hadn’t felt the increase in sound from the devastating punches he had been landing on the poor mountain for days, but she knew that reality up close would be much different.
Suddenly, a faint yellow, mysterious Aura appeared around his hands, only covering his fists. He recognized it as the first level without even needing to read the message from his system.

But unlike his master—who could cover her entire body and weapon with Aura—and whose intensity was many times stronger, his was limited. He punched again, maintaining his Aura with full force, while Rajin’s Descent remained continuously active.

The result made his eyes widen in shock, as the difference was immense. A thought crossed his mind. If Seraphine had managed to catch him that day, he would have had no chance of stopping her attack, no matter how much mana he had poured into his ice element.
Now he believed it was only because of his space element that he was able to stop her.

He realized how overpowered the space element actually was—it could render even Aura useless if he had enough mana, as he had used three times more total mana than she had to make her completely immovable.

chapters.title: Chapter 94: Using Epic Ranked Sword for the first time
paragraphs: Leon looked at the 10-meter-deep hole in front of him, which had an entrance 20 meters wide. It was caused by his full-power strike using his Rajin’s Descent Grandmaster rank, Mana Body Enhancement—which was always active at Master’s rank—and his Aura around his fist, which he had just grasped.
’I built a tunnel with a single punch.’

Despite the fact that he wasn’t practicing Mana Body Enhancement, focusing on increasing its rank, it still made quite a lot of improvement just by being used all this while he was focusing on reaching Grandmaster rank in Rajin’s Descent.
He could feel it now, Rajin’s Descent was now making his physical capabilities thrice as strong—a massive boost.
With his Master’s rank Mana Enhancement, along with Rajin’s Descent and Aura, he had become a terrifying existence. He thought he could bring down the mountain in front of him just by punching alone.
Because of how big the damage his single punch alone caused, his single punch could obliterate any level 10 Apprentice rank in the Lower Domain—that’s what he believed.
If it was true or not, he would find that out later.
Even then, he wasn’t stopping now. Once his training was over, he would become very strong, and he was excited for that.

He continued the training, moving onto the Skybreak Draw technique. As for Mana Body Enhancement, he was keeping it on all the time. Even if the progress was slow because of not giving it the focus, it was still there.
Another year had passed inside.
The previous mountain was completely gone now, as he was now standing in front of another mountain, which was 400 meters tall, twice the size of the previous one.
In his hand was his Uncommon rank blade. Leon was just standing still in place on the mountain, where no markings were present, unlike the other sides, where deep slashes were present.

He had just reached the Grandmaster rank in Skybreaker Draw, and he was ready to test out its power. He had even learned to make his Aura form around his blade, as his understanding of lightning Aura increased.
He could also cover some parts of his body, like arms and legs, but not the whole body, just yet.

He was in his strongest state right now. Rajin’s Descent was active, as thin strands of golden lightning made ripples around his body. Mana Body Enhancement, while showing no effect on the outside, had been making him many times stronger from the inside.
He was calm as he gazed at the tall mountain in front of him, his one hand always on the sheathed sword, his small frame like an ant in front of the towering mountain.

Taking a deep breath, the mana inside his body stirred. In a flash, he drew his blade out of its sheath to slash at the mountain with full strength. In between, a yellow lightning Aura formed around the blade before the attack connected.
The Skybreaker Draw doesn’t have any flashy moves like Rajin’s Descent—just a simple draw, which is a strong and lightning-fast attack.
The vertical slash connected to the mountain started slicing the rocky surface of the mountain like butter.
A half-meter-wide slash appeared on the mountain, reaching almost 200 meters deep, half its length. Only then did it stop. All of this happened in less than a millisecond.

Leon looked at the attack, which almost cut this big mountain in half. This attack was very strong. In his strongest form, without the Skybreaker Draw, he could never hope to achieve such deadly results unless he used too much of his mana to attack with concentrated force.

But its mana cost would be high, unlike the technique, which was very cost-effective. Even as the technique’s rank increased, a bit more mana was required to use it. Still, he could maintain his state for hours, considering his super-fast mana recovery.
’If I only had Grandmaster rank Mana Body Enhancement, I would have been able to cut the mountain in half with one swing.’
He looked at the sword in his hand, which crumbled after the last attack. It lasted longer than he had anticipated.
But Leon wasn’t worried, as he took out a sword from his inventory, which looked nothing more than a fancy sword. He caught it with one hand.
It appeared with a quiet flash—long, sharp, and dangerously sleek. A matte black blade in a dark sheath, with a polished silver handle that looked like it came from a noble’s collection.

It was the Blade of Convenient Sharpness—the Epic-ranked sword. Leon was able to lift it when he had reached Grandmaster rank in Rajin’s Descent. Along with the help of Mana Body Enhancement, he could lift it, but it felt quite heavy. For wielding, he would get tired quite quickly while using it.
But he knew that when he reached Grandmaster rank in Mana Body Enhancement, he would be able to wield it much more easily.

He hoisted it around his waist to use the Skybreaker Draw. He could do so while drawing it from his hands, but this posture was easier for him because of the sword’s weight. It was still too heavy. He thought he would be able to wield it for five minutes.

It was the first time he was trying out this sword. Leon was excited, and he could also feel the excitement coming through the blade itself, through the connection he had formed since the last time he had lifted it up with his one hand.
It cut his hand despite being only in its sheath and absorbed his blood. Since that time, he could feel a strong connection with the blade through his soul and felt every emotion it felt.
Unlike previously, when it showed emotion by trying to put pressure on his body somehow.
Leon was in the same place. He took a deep breath, as this time he had to push himself to the limit to make the slash.
Another slash happened as his hand moved lightning fast, using his full strength, using Skybreaker Draw. This time, it was a horizontal slash, not a vertical slash.
After making the slash, his hand nearly rotated itself due to the momentum and weight of the sword.
He barely stopped it, and then he looked at the sight in front of him, which made his entire body shudder.

sentences.text: Leon looked at the 10-meter-deep hole in front of him, which had an entrance 20 meters wide.

It was caused by his full-power strike using his Rajin’s Descent Grandmaster rank, Mana Body Enhancement—which was always active at Master’s rank—and his Aura around his fist, which he had just grasped.
’I built a tunnel with a single punch.’

Despite the fact that he wasn’t practicing Mana Body Enhancement, focusing on increasing its rank, it still made quite a lot of improvement just by being used all this while he was focusing on reaching Grandmaster rank in Rajin’s Descent.
He could feel it now, Rajin’s Descent was now making his physical capabilities thrice as strong—a massive boost.
With his Master’s rank Mana Enhancement, along with Rajin’s Descent and Aura, he had become a terrifying existence.
He thought he could bring down the mountain in front of him just by punching alone.
Because of how big the damage his single punch alone caused, his single punch could obliterate any level 10 Apprentice rank in the Lower Domain—that’s what he believed.
If it was true or not, he would find that out later.
Even then, he wasn’t stopping now.
Once his training was over, he would become very strong, and he was excited for that.
He continued the training, moving onto the Skybreak Draw technique.
As for Mana Body Enhancement, he was keeping it on all the time.
Even if the progress was slow because of not giving it the focus, it was still there.
Another year had passed inside.
The previous mountain was completely gone now, as he was now standing in front of another mountain, which was 400 meters tall, twice the size of the previous one.
In his hand was his Uncommon rank blade.
Leon was just standing still in place on the mountain, where no markings were present, unlike the other sides, where deep slashes were present.
He had just reached the Grandmaster rank in Skybreaker Draw, and he was ready to test out its power.
He had even learned to make his Aura form around his blade, as his understanding of lightning Aura increased.
He could also cover some parts of his body, like arms and legs, but not the whole body, just yet.
He was in his strongest state right now.
Rajin’s Descent was active, as thin strands of golden lightning made ripples around his body.
Mana Body Enhancement, while showing no effect on the outside, had been making him many times stronger from the inside.
He was calm as he gazed at the tall mountain in front of him, his one hand always on the sheathed sword, his small frame like an ant in front of the towering mountain.

In a flash, he drew his blade out of its sheath to slash at the mountain with full strength.

All of this happened in less than a millisecond.

chapters.title: Chapter 95: Arriving at the City Gate of Hemsburg
paragraphs: A mountain that was once standing tall and majestic now had a meter-wide slash from its very top to bottom, splitting the whole mountain in half with adeep, thunderouscrack. He could even cross the mountain if he wanted.
It reminded him of certain mythological stories about making a path in the sea, but he had done so with a mountain in a single strike.

He even felt little to no resistance when the strike connected to the rocky mountain surface—unlike the time when he would use the Uncommonly ranked sword. He even felt that if there was something else behind the mountain instead of nothing, it would have also gotten the brunt of the attack.
Seraphine, watching at a distance, seeing the mountain split by a clean cut like a single sword strike, had her mouth hang open, as it didn’t even look like it could be done by a human.
As it was the first time for her, she had seen such unfathomable power.

She knew now the forbidden mist wouldn’t be able to stop Leon at all. After the festival ended, she had decided there was no point in staying in this Lower Domain any longer. They would depart for the Middle Domain.

For Leon, it had been 2 years and 3 months, but for her, it had only been 9 months. It would still take her much more time to reach Grandmaster level in Mana Body Enhancement, and that was not all, as she was regularly training her Level 1 Aura, which was also showing slow but steady progress.
If she reached Level 2 in her Aura, she knew she would be able to hold on her own easily—not at the level of her monstrous disciple, but she would be quite strong.
She was quite happy at the rate at which she was making progress. She had already given up on comparing herself to Leon now.
The sight of such a tall mountain split in two by his sword strike only made her see him with pride and reverence.
Seven days had passed in the outside world.

Leon had spent a total of eighteen years inside the dimensional space just for training. It could have been nineteen years, but they had to come out of the dimension space for food and other basic needs. Also, in between every week, they would have romantic sessions together.
The door of the carriage opened suddenly with a sharpclack, making both Leon and Seraphine open their eyes. Having been inside, they could detect if someone was close to them.
"My lady, there is a problem outside," Kaela hurried to say those words, with an annoyed expression on her face, anger visible on her features.
Just as Leon opened his eyes for a moment, his pressure leaked out—wooomph—making Kaela grit her teeth as she almost came to her knees, if it wasn’t for Leon controlling it in less than a second.
Kaela looked at Young Master Leon weirdly, as the pressure came from him, but she chose to ignore it, as neither her lady nor even Young Master brought it up.

Leon, who had made the slip-up, had decided he had to train for at least a month inside the time dimension in his physical form to get used to everything he had learned—because his little slip-up could kill people, not intentionally, but unintentionally.
For Seraphine, she wasn’t much affected by the pressure, but she felt it clearly.
But she knew this was nothing but a drop in the ocean compared to what she had witnessed in the past six years of her training.

She succeeded in achieving Grandmaster level in Mana Body Enhancement, but for Level 2 Aura, she was very close to reaching it—but not there yet. She felt like she needed a strong opponent to bring it out like the last time.

She looked at Kaela, who looked troubled. They had entered the Kingdom of Champagne a day ago, and now their carriage was stopped at the gate of their capital city, Hemsburg, which she could see from the window.
"What’s the problem, Kaela? Why weren’t we let inside the city?" Seraphine asked, her voice sharp.

She could guess what was happening. It happened later than she anticipated, as the Duke’s son must have been aware of their date for quite a while. He must be plotting something and would be furious to strike.
’So they made their move when we were in the heart of their territory. Pretty clever, but it won’t change anything.’

"My lady, even after seeing your crest and hearing your name, they insisted on checking the carriage, saying they have been given orders to check anyone who enters the city regardless of their rank, as there have been rumors inside the city that around the time of the festival some thugs are trying to cause chaos in the city—from their intel."

Even Kaela knew this was bullshit and knew why this was happening. She was a bit worried too, as no matter how strong her lady was, it was not a smart move to enter your enemy’s territory with so few of her people.
"Should we go back, my lady? The festival isn’t important enough to fall into such an obvious trap." She didn’t want Young Master Leon to become the target of this scheme.
Seraphine’s confident voice sounded. "Don’t worry, Kaela. I know what you are worried about, but I will handle everything just fine."
Kaela didn’t question her after hearing this—no matter how unbelievable it sounded—as she knew her lady’s words were never empty.
Leon had a bright smile on his face when he heard all this, as it would give him even more reasons to act against them. He knew he was being targeted, and he was thrilled to know that.
As he accompanied Seraphine to the guards, walking on her right side—not behind her, but along with her.

Guards who were seeing the infamous Commander of the Duskmoor, who was feared all over the world, known for being one of the strongest in the world—seeing her unfathomable presence, every step filled with power and grace—tap... tap... tap—her boots hitting the stone ground with dreadful elegance.
They cursed their luck, as her cold face and sharp eyes told them any mishap and she would kill them for sure.
All the guards had only one thought in their minds, their faces pale:
’Who is the fucking bastard trying to make our lives hell? We don’t get paid enough to handle this shit.’

chapters.title: Chapter 96: The Guard Leader Catching Stray
paragraphs: Guards could also see that there was a tall young man with silver-white hair walking beside Commander Seraphine, as if he were her equal. He had a domineering and mystical presence due to his sharp features and mysterious eyes.
He also exuded a pressure of authority, just like the commander. They had guessed anyone walking beside Commander Seraphine would not be a pushover either.

But what could they do? That was their luck, as this was the same description they had been given for the leader of the thugs who were going to cause chaos inside the capital city when the festival took place.
That was the order they had received from the higher-ups.

But they knew it was complete gibberish. Who would dare to do something like that in the most secure city in the entire world? Security was extremely tight, especially during festival times. And monsters among humans walked in the disguise of normal people—the so-called Awakeners. The city was full of them.

Whoever had given the order definitely had some animosity toward the silver-white-haired handsome young man beside the commander, and they knew who it might be. The story of the commander and the duke’s eldest son’s open announcement to the world was known to everyone.

They were stuck between fire and a cliff. Knowing the duke’s eldest son was behind this put so much pressure on them that they had to act—even if they didn’t like it—despite the commander accompanying him.
They were Awakeners, and the guards believed they could subdue him—only if the commander didn’t act up.

All of them were hoping to convince her with words, because no matter what, she was still in their kingdom’s capital city—their home ground. The upper hand was supposed to be in their pocket, not hers. Even though she was one of the strongest people in the world, she had to be careful around here.

Seraphine and Leon reached them. Behind them were eight knights of Seraphine—five women and three men—all of them with their hands on the hilts of their blades, as they could feel the tense atmosphere emitted by the guard who seemed to be in charge of everyone.
"Greetings, Esteemed Lightning Commander Seraphine."
Seraphine didn’t even give him a nod, more curious about what lie that scheming bastard, the duke’s son, had cooked up now.

The guard leader clearly sensed she was not even acknowledging their existence, but it didn’t affect him, as he continued—trying to imitate a heavy voice to let her know the severity of the situation—and also didn’t forget to mention the termhigher-upsmany times during his explanation.
Even while he tried to maintain a calm composure, after his explanation was done, the shaking in his hands was a clear reminder of how nervous he was.

He explained everything about how the young man beside her matched the description of the thug. He didn’t directly say to hand him over, but kept mentioning it was a very high-level order, and that she shouldn’t make things difficult for them, repeating the same message while trying to redirect her anger away from him.
The guard leader was holding his breath, hoping she wouldn’t make things difficult for them.
’This is it, huh? Pretty nasty... but I’m not gonna hold back anymore.’
"So you’re saying the man beside me matched the description of the thug you wanted to find. Is that correct?" Her tone was sharper than ever, her cold eyes looking at him as if he were a bug.
"Ye—"
"ARRRGH!!!"
The overwhelming pain came before the guard even realized what had happened. His body hit the ground as he frantically moved like a worm.
Thud.
His right hand had hit the ground.
From his shoulder, his whole arm had been cut. The other guards took out their weapons in response, along with the eight knights behind Seraphine.

But the guards’ legs were shaking. None of them had seen how their leader—the strongest among them—was now on the ground with his entire arm severed from his body, blood leaking as he clutched it tightly, screaming his lungs out.
ARRRGH!

Even though their number was around fifty—including those rushing there after hearing the scream—not a single one of them had the confidence to face her. Death seemed inevitable if they acted against her, regardless of their numbers.
"ARGGHH! BASTARDS, QUICKLY TAKE ME TO THE CHURCH OF LIFE! I WILL DIE, YOU RETARDS!!"
The scream of their leader made them focus on him.
Four guards came up, trying to pick up the leader to take him to the Church of Life for emergency treatment.
But they stopped in their tracks, hearing a cold and ruthless voice.
"I’m still not done with him."
The four guards froze in place after hearing the devil’s voice. They dared not try to touch their leader. They valued their lives.
They only showed pity in their eyes while looking at their leader, who was bleeding profusely, squirming on the ground, and screaming.

A few days prior, when this mission came to their guard leader, they were jealous, as he was given an advance payment of 50 gold coins before even catching the thug, and promised a promotion and one platinum coin after the capture.

They had thought the leader had hit the jackpot. But now, they realized he was only a sacrificial pawn for the upper nobles. It definitely wasn’t a coincidence that this mission came just as the silver-white-haired man arrived with the infamous lightning commander, knowing their duke’s obsession with her.

"P-Please ma’am... l-let me go, I beg of you! I-I will die if they don’t take me quickly..." he weakly said these words while still on the ground—his previous demeanor, trying to put up a brave front, subtly reminding her she was in their kingdom’s capital—was gone, he could cry at any second.
Now, in front of her, only a man remained—begging for his life, not wanting to die.
Seraphine ignored his pleading and continued.

"Do you know this silver-white-haired young man is with me? Wasn’t he walking alongside me enough to tell you that? Be grateful that you are still breathing. Your earlier words were a direct affront to my honor."
"I’d say I’ve even been too kind today."
The eight knights behind Seraphine nodded in unison, agreeing with their lady’s words, as she had indeed been kind today.

chapters.title: Chapter 97: Brilliant Plan
paragraphs: The guard leader, writhing on the ground from the pain, witnessed everything with his own eyes—the reaction of the eight knights behind the commander proved that she really was telling the truth when she said she had been kind today.

He realized that his luck was truly terrible. The woman in front of him was far crazier than he had imagined. Now, all he wanted was to get as far away from her as possible. He no longer cared about catching the silver-white-haired young man beside her, who was watching everything with an amused look on his face.
The leader thoughthe was crazy, too. He was dying here, and not one of them showed any sympathy for a dying man caught in this mess because of a little greed.

He should have been suspicious when he was offered such a large bonus just for accepting the task. The description didn’t match any known powerful figure, so he had let greed overtake his logical mind.
He regretted his decision with every fiber of his being now.
"M-Ma’am, I-I’m really, really sorry if my earlier words caused any harm to your reputation... Please forgive me. I-It’s all a misunderstanding caused by the higher-ups..."
There was bitterness in his voice as he mentioned the higher-ups.
"T-The young master with you can enter the city without any checks. Forgive my mistake, please. How can anyone with ma’am’s be a thug...?"
"Just let them carry me—I’ll really die. I-I don’t want to die. I’m not even married y-yet. Please..."
He even used his bloody hand to take out a pouch from around his waist—rather than holding onto his wound—and offered it to the commander, hoping she would accept it as compensation.
"Please accept this, m-ma’am..."
The pouch contained 52 gold coins, 90 silver coins, and a couple of bronze coins—his earnings and savings.
Seraphine was satisfied with the apology, knowing he was merely a pawn used by the duke’s son and had been caught off guard. He had already paid with one of his hands. Her cold voice sounded again.
"Okay, you’re forgiven for now. But if you ever get in my way again, I will kill you. And I don’t need your compensation."
The guard leader felt relieved when he heard she wouldn’t take the money. That meant he could at least enjoy a decent retirement.

But Leon, beside her, wasn’t going to let it go. The pouch looked heavy with coins. His hand moved in a blur, and he caught it. He didn’t care about the blood and opened the pouch. Just one look at the many gold and silver coins inside, and he knew he’d hit the jackpot.
The weight of the pouch gone from his waist, the leader’s soul felt shattered. He could see his retirement fund in the hands of the silver-haired young man.
It was over now—but at least he had kept his life. Even with one hand, as an Awakener with an intact mana core, he could still earn decent money.
Seraphine continued.
"My disciple will take the compensation, as you targeted him. Now disappear from my sight before I change my mind."
"Thank you, m-ma’am..."
His entire demeanor changed as he glared at the four guards standing nearby.
"Quickly take me to the Church of Life, you fools! Are you waiting for me to die!?"
The guards picked up the leader and his severed hand as they left. The other guards thanked their luck and sighed in relief—grateful he had handled the situation without worsening it.
Had he acted foolishly, all of them might have lost their lives.
Seraphine and Leon returned to the carriage, while the knights mounted their horses again.
Leon discreetly stored the pouch in his inventory when no eyes were on him, and water formed around his hands, washing away the blood.
After boarding the carriage, he and Seraphine didn’t return to the dimensional space just yet. He knew, from what Seraphine had told him, that the festival would begin in two days.

Then he remembered something—he had forgotten to tell Seraphine about the existence of theCosmic ShopandCosmic Chat. He had to bring it up because rejecting even small coin exchanges meant rejecting causality itself.
They were too precious to miss.
Seraphine’s hands were wrapped around his as her head rested peacefully on his shoulder.
"Seraphine, I forgot to tell you something about my system. The thing is..."
He finished speaking.

She’d never thought there could be more to his system than what he’d already told her—because what he’d revealed was already overwhelming. Now, hearing about the overpowered shop that allowed him to buy treasures of the same rank as the ones he owned—using a strange currency calledCausality, earned by exchanging time—was beyond her imagination.
He told her about a certain item that increased mana by 300 after a single use—double the amount of her current mana. And that wasn’t all. He spoke of many godly treasures sold by powerful entities.

She realized why he had taken the money from the guard earlier. He wasn’t lacking funds. If he had asked, she would have given him more than enough. But now she doubted it would ever beenough—not after hearing how much platinum he had exchanged for only 289,000 causality.
That amount alone was far more than the total wealth she owned in coin. But her wealth wasn’t limited to money—there were other valuables stored in her treasury, hidden beneath her mansion.
Once they returned, she had decided she would exchangeeverythingshe had for this "Causality" he spoke of.

If possible, she wanted to buy high-level technique scrolls—because unlike skill stones, technique scrolls had no limitations. They could be passed down to different people and can even be stored inside into paper by a person who had a good understanding of the technique, as the direct transfer was too dangerous of method for average people.
It would not only increase their strength—but it would also become the foundation of their future empire.
Even if they sold only a part of a scroll—not even the full version—it would still generate enough revenue and treasure to earn more causality, potentially surpassing the original cost.
It was, in her eyes, the best investment—killing three birds with one stone.

She didn’t hold back and shared her full idea with him. Leon gave her a wide smile in return, wrapping her in a long hug and kissing her deeply in appreciation of her brilliant plan—making her feel proud of herself.
