chapters.title: Chapter 98: Arriving at Capital city Hemsburg
paragraphs: Leon, through the window, noticed the bustling city outside. Duskmoor seemed like a village compared to this crowd. People were constantly moving through the streets, and large shops and tall buildings appeared frequently.

Guards could be seen every hundred meters along the road. The streets were well-made, with lamps placed every few steps. He hadn’t seen a single beggar in the city so far, which surprised him—Duskmoor, even if few, still had beggars.
But this city felt too grand—or was it just a façade? He didn’t know.
Their carriage stopped in front of a house.

A sleek, three-story house with marble walls, tall windows, and a black iron gate. Golden lights glowed from inside, and a quiet fountain trickled by the entrance—elegant and refined, even in the heart of the city.
Seraphine and Leon got off the carriage and entered the house, followed by the knights.
She ordered them to relax, to do whatever they wanted, as she didn’t need them for now. The journey had been long, and they must be tired.
After entering the master bedroom with Seraphine, Leon quickly expressed his intent to enter the dimensional space in his physical body to gain proper control over his newly awakened strength.
Seraphine wanted to follow him as well—she needed to adjust to her power, too. But her condition was better than his, as she hadn’t experienced such astronomical growth.
She had become many times stronger, yes—but Leon? She didn’t even know. Hundreds of times stronger? Perhaps even more.
Transcendent-rank mastery in a technique that was far too powerful.
Other than adjusting to her strength, there was something else she wanted to do with him as well.
Both of them entered the portal and arrived at the familiar place—there should have been tall, rocky mountains everywhere in sight.

She didn’t know if her Leon had a grudge against mountains, butnot a single one remained. Wherever she looked, only their broken remains could be seen. Most of the land for kilometers around was littered with craters. It looked like a devastating earthquake had struck the area, leaving behind a scene of destruction.
But within a 30-meter radius, the bed, table, chairs, sofa, and bathtub remained untouched by the surrounding chaos. That was the place they used to relax from time to time.
Her training also caused destruction, butnotto the level of destroying entire mountains or reshaping the landscape for kilometers around.
Leon vanished from his spot after saying goodbye and reappeared five kilometers away from her, beginning his practice to adjust to his new strength using his real body.
One thing surprised him—the vast, unchanging terrain of rocky mountains and treacherous paths in every direction.
If he wanted a new training partner—another mountain to play with—he had to travel several kilometers just to find one.
Forty days had passed inside the dimensional space. Leon now felt confident in his control over his new strength. He no longer feared accidentally killing someone.

Feeling hungry, he decided to return to Seraphine and have dinner with her. He called it dinner because the sky never changed—it always looked like sunset, even though there was no sun or moon to begin with.
He still remembered her shocked face when she saw the Infinite Spoon of Soup in action for the first time, a month ago.
He had tried to use it with mana, which he had never done before. The result was staggering: the amount of soup it produced in a single second increased dramatically.
It didn’tneedmana to work, but with it, the treasure felt like it was meant to feed not just a village, but a town, a city, a kingdom, an empire, or even the world itself.
The speed at which it produced soup depended heavily on how much mana was provided.
And with the abundance of mana here, it could already produce hundreds of liters of delicious, nutritious soup in just a few minutes. So, giving it mana directly yielded even better results.

After reaching closer to their make-shift home without any roof, he noticed Seraphine wasn’t training anymore, instead could see her in her sexy nighty, flaunting her curves, she even looked him in his eyes and licked her lips seductively.
He didn’t care about the dinner anymore, as an even better dinner was inviting him.
Arriving in front of in a flash in front on her.

Seraphine, draped in a black silk nightgown that shimmered with every movement, hugging her curves, slit high enough to reveal the bare line of her thigh. She turned when Leon arrived, her lips curling in a slow, knowing smile.
"You’re staring," she said softly.
"I always do," Leon replied, crossing the room. He slid an arm under her knees and one behind her back, lifting her effortlessly into his arms.
She let out a breathy laugh, brushing her fingers along his neck. "So eager, My Leon?"
"I’ve been patient enough," he murmured, kissing her temple. "Tonight, I’m not letting you rest."
He laid her down onto the bed, the silk of her nightgown sliding against her skin as she leaned back on her elbows, legs slightly parted. "Then don’t," she whispered, voice low and inviting.
Leon climbed over her, pressing her down with his weight, hand sliding up her thigh, beneath the fabric, fingers brushing her warmth.
"No underwear," he noted, smirking.
"I thought it would save time."
He pulled the gown up to her waist, revealing all of her. "You’re soaked already."
Her breath caught. "Maybe I’ve been waiting all day... wondering how rough you’d be tonight."
Leon kissed her deeply—hungry, claiming—and entered her in one slow, smooth thrust. Her gasp melted into a moan, her back arching beneath him.
Schlick... slap... slap...
Ahhn~
Ahhn~
He moved with deep, steady strokes, every thrust deliberate, pressing into her completely, dragging against every inch.
"You feel incredible," he breathed. "So warm... so tight."
She cupped his face, pulling him in for another kiss. "Then don’t hold back. Make me forget everything but you."
He did.
His rhythm quickened, hips snapping into hers as the bed rocked beneath them. Her moans grew higher, her legs locking around his waist.
"Gods, Leon—keep going... angh~ you feel so good."
"yes~ faster! fuck me hard~"
"Look at you," he whispered, kissing her neck. "Writhing under me... begging without even realizing it."
Slap! Schlick! Slap!
He flipped her over, pulled her hips up, and slid back in from behind. She gasped, grabbing the sheets as he filled her again, deeper this time.
"You like this?" he asked, gripping her waist tightly. "Me taking my time? Letting you feel everything?"
She glanced over her shoulder, eyes dazed. "I love it... love how you make me yours every time..."
Leon leaned forward, lips brushing her ear. "I’ll keep going until you forget your own name."
Time blurred. Position after position, her body trembled under his control—legs spread, pinned wrists, her head tilted back in ecstasy, the sound of wet skin and soft moans echoing endlessly.
Even when her voice broke and her limbs went limp, her eyes still burned with desire.
Until the very end.
Her body trembled one last time—overwhelmed, exhausted, spent. She let out a soft moan as her eyes fluttered shut, her lips parting in a final breathless sigh.
Leon held her close, his breathing heavy, her body soft in his arms.
She had passed out with a smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 99: Exploration Begins
paragraphs: Both of them slept together for the night in each other’s embrace, peacefully.

The next day, they woke up and took a bath together. They had their breakfast inside the dimensional space, consisting of soup from the Infinite Spoon of Soup, beef jerky, different fruits, some snacks, and drinks.
Leon heard Seraphine’s voice from the other end of the small table as she looked directly at him.

"Leon, you’ve gotten used to your strength. We should be getting out of here now. My training ended a few weeks ago—I was just waiting for you to finish. However, I think we should spend more time inside. There’s something important we need to do here."
She paused for a moment, a smile tugging at her beautiful lips.
Leon didn’t interrupt her. He knew her well enough to tell that she was about to say something important, though he had no idea what it might be.
A thought arose in his mind.
Does she want another fight?
But he didn’t want that to happen, especially while they were in their real bodies. He was too strong now—he didn’t think she would be able to put up a fight at all, unlike before.
It wasn’t that she had become weaker, quite the opposite, she was many times stronger now, but—it was just that he had become too powerful.
Still, he let her finish.
"We’re going on an exploration mission to find a piece of land perfectly suited for our future empire."
What? Future empire?
"What are you talking about, Seraphine? What future empire?" Leon asked her, confusion written clearly on his face.
He wanted her to explain more before he said anything. Just because he had such a large space—one whose size he didn’t even fully know—didn’t mean he intended to bring outsiders here.
Seraphine ignored the caution written on his face. She was sure that once he heard her full idea, he would never dismiss it—because of how foolproof her plan was.
"Leon, you have the Dimensional Hourglass and the Spoon of Infinite Soup. So let’s think of it this way..."
After she finished speaking, she remained silent, a confident look on her face, her head held higher than usual. A small smile graced her lips, exuding assurance in her idea.

She didn’t even think it was a hard idea to conceive. Implementing it was the harder part. Besides, the only reason Leon hadn’t thought of this himself, despite having all the pieces of the puzzle, was because of how cautious he was.

Leon was hooked by the first question she had asked him:"Do you think I would even be able to get out of this place if you didn’t allow me to?"And the answer was:No. She would never be able to unless he opened the portal himself.
Which meant that anyone who came inside was basically his prisoner—no one could leave unless he allowed it.

That wasn’t all. She had also pointed out that time here moved a thousand times faster than outside, and said,"What if we left only a couple hundred people here? In one year outside, it would be a thousand years in here."That was more than enough time for a new civilization to be formed from scratch.

But in their case, they would be guiding and helping it grow from the shadows, making the process faster. The main problem of food was already solved by his overpowered treasure—the Infinite Spoon of Soup.
And even that wouldn’t be needed forever. As civilization grew, they developed their own methods of food production.
The perks were endless. He could have thousands, hundreds of thousands, or even millions of people under his command.
In here, he would be like a king—or an emperor—to them.
Only those he deemed worthy would be allowed to leave and help him in the outside world.
The idea alone made his breath hitch slightly from the sheer excitement. The possibilities were limitless.
The sooner he started this mission, the better it would be for him.

He also now understood why she had told him to buy techniques from the Cosmic Shop before anything else. Besides the fact that incomplete versions could be resold to gain more Causality—and that both of them could use them—she had hidden the fact that those techniques could become the foundation of their empire.

He couldn’t help but shower her with endless praise for five whole minutes. He knew, given his cautious personality, that he wouldn’t have come up with this idea for years. He might have had the idea eventually, but she had saved him a massive amount of time.
His Seraphine was brilliant.
Seraphine took all the praise like a champion, smiling gleefully the entire time, and even made him repeat the praises she liked the most.
Both of them got up from their seats, ready to depart to explore what lay beyond the vast, rocky mountains.

"Let’s go, Seraphine. Uh, I’d be much faster if I did it like this." He stepped closer to her and picked her up in a princess carry without warning, making Seraphine slightly surprised for a second, then she wrapped her arms around his neck.
"You should wrap your body with your Aura—just in case." His voice was serious as he said those words.
Seraphine did as she was told without question, knowing how much of a freak her disciple really was. It was definitely needed for her safety.

She even felt another layer of lightning Aura wrap around her. Her eyes trembled slightly upon realizing how close it was to reaching Level 2, just like hers. She didn’t know he had achieved such results in Aura.

But it didn’t stop there—two other unfamiliar Auras wrapped around her as well, making her slightly panic inside. She had been training far away from him, so unlike the beginning of their training, she hadn’t witnessed how far he had progressed.
The only reminder of his strength was the tremors—like earthquakes she would feel from time to time.

Even if those two unfamiliar Auras hadn’t yet reached Level 2, they still reminded her just how monstrous her disciple really was. Holding three different Auras, when most people struggled to master even one.

Leon didn’t interrupt her.
He knew her well enough to tell that she was about to say something important, though he had no idea what it might be.
A thought arose in his mind.
Does she want another fight?
But he didn’t want that to happen, especially while they were in their real bodies.
He was too strong now—he didn’t think she would be able to put up a fight at all, unlike before.
It wasn’t that she had become weaker, quite the opposite, she was many times stronger now, but—it was just that he had become too powerful.
Still, he let her finish.
"We’re going on an exploration mission to find a piece of land perfectly suited for our future empire."
What?
Future empire?
"What are you talking about, Seraphine?
What future empire?" Leon asked her, confusion written clearly on his face.
He wanted her to explain more before he said anything.
Just because he had such a large space—one whose size he didn’t even fully know—didn’t mean he intended to bring outsiders here.
Seraphine ignored the caution written on his face.
She was sure that once he heard her full idea, he would never dismiss it—because of how foolproof her plan was.
"Leon, you have the Dimensional Hourglass and the Spoon of Infinite Soup.
So let’s think of it this way..."
After she finished speaking, she remained silent, a confident look on her face, her head held higher than usual.
A small smile graced her lips, exuding assurance in her idea.
She didn’t even think it was a hard idea to conceive.
Implementing it was the harder part.
Besides, the only reason Leon hadn’t thought of this himself, despite having all the pieces of the puzzle, was because of how cautious he was.
Leon was hooked by the first question she had asked him:"Do you think I would even be able to get out of this place if you didn’t allow me to?"And the answer was:No.
She would never be able to unless he opened the portal himself.
Which meant that anyone who came inside was basically his prisoner—no one could leave unless he allowed it.
That wasn’t all.
She had also pointed out that time here moved a thousand times faster than outside, and said,"What if we left only a couple hundred people here?
In one year outside, it would be a thousand years in here."That was more than enough time for a new civilization to be formed from scratch.
But in their case, they would be guiding and helping it grow from the shadows, making the process faster.
The main problem of food was already solved by his overpowered treasure—the Infinite Spoon of Soup.
And even that wouldn’t be needed forever.
As civilization grew, they developed their own methods of food production.
The perks were endless.
He could have thousands, hundreds of thousands, or even millions of people under his command.
In here, he would be like a king—or an emperor—to them.
Only those he deemed worthy would be allowed to leave and help him in the outside world.
The idea alone made his breath hitch slightly from the sheer excitement.
The possibilities were limitless.
The sooner he started this mission, the better it would be for him.
He also now understood why she had told him to buy techniques from the Cosmic Shop before anything else.

Besides the fact that incomplete versions could be resold to gain more Causality—and that both of them could use them—she had hidden the fact that those techniques could become the foundation of their empire.
He couldn’t help but shower her with endless praise for five whole minutes.
He knew, given his cautious personality, that he wouldn’t have come up with this idea for years.
He might have had the idea eventually, but she had saved him a massive amount of time.
His Seraphine was brilliant.
Seraphine took all the praise like a champion, smiling gleefully the entire time, and even made him repeat the praises she liked the most.
Both of them got up from their seats, ready to depart to explore what lay beyond the vast, rocky mountains.
"Let’s go, Seraphine.

Uh, I’d be much faster if I did it like this." He stepped closer to her and picked her up in a princess carry without warning, making Seraphine slightly surprised for a second, then she wrapped her arms around his neck.
"You should wrap your body with your Aura—just in case." His voice was serious as he said those words.
Seraphine did as she was told without question, knowing how much of a freak her disciple really was.
It was definitely needed for her safety.
She even felt another layer of lightning Aura wrap around her.
Her eyes trembled slightly upon realizing how close it was to reaching Level 2, just like hers.
She didn’t know he had achieved such results in Aura.
But it didn’t stop there—two other unfamiliar Auras wrapped around her as well, making her slightly panic inside.
She had been training far away from him, so unlike the beginning of their training, she hadn’t witnessed how far he had progressed.
The only reminder of his strength was the tremors—like earthquakes she would feel from time to time.
Even if those two unfamiliar Auras hadn’t yet reached Level 2, they still reminded her just how monstrous her disciple really was.
Holding three different Auras, when most people struggled to master even one.

chapters.title: Chapter 100: Falling Rizz
paragraphs: Leon had noticed the shock on her face, but he didn’t say anything and only found her adorable, as he had thought she had gotten used to being shocked by him, but that didn’t seem to be the case.
The mana inside his body surged through every part of his body, as the Transcendent-ranked Mana Body Enhancement was at work, filling his body with endless strength.

But he didn’t just stop there, as the lightning energy inside his body traveled through various intricate patterns. No flashy ripple or thin strands of lightning element moved around his body like in the Grandmaster-ranked version, but only a single golden thunderbolt symbol appeared between his temples.

He was careful not to release any of the natural pressure coming from him as he used these Transcendent-rank techniques on her. His practice over the past 40 days didn’t go unnoticed, as she didn’t feel a thing—but her senses told her that her disciple was unfathomably strong right now, as she gazed at the golden lightning symbol between his temples.

She knew he was using the Transcendent-rank Rajin’s Descent Technique. Knowing how difficult it was to reach the Grandmaster rank in mana enhancement technique—even with her previous years of training—it had taken her five full years of training. It might as well be called ten years, as in the conscious state, she didn’t need any rest or sleep.
And the Transcendent rank felt too far away. She couldn’t even put a number on how many years it would take her to achieve it, because of how big the gap really was.
Leon smiled faintly and asked her,
"Are you ready for the ride?"
She was not nervous and nodded her head at his words, as she knew he would never let her get harmed.
In the next second, the ground beneath him cracked. With the booming sound of air pressure, Leon’s body launched forward, with Seraphine clinging tightly to his neck.
He had made sure to steer away from their makeshift home; otherwise, everything might have been destroyed just by his launch alone.
Only a few seconds had passed, and now Seraphine, in his arms, couldn’t even register how fast they were actually moving—everything was just a blur to her vision.
Leon stopped.
Which made Seraphine a bit confused, as only a few seconds had passed. Why did he stop? They couldn’t have gotten far.

She looked around and only saw his devastation everywhere—craters all over, mountains reduced to crumbling rocks, thousand-meter-long sword strikes on the ground, meters wide and deep like cliffs. She could only see darkness inside them, unable to tell how deep they went.
She knew it was his training spot, which should be around five kilometers away from their home. She looked back but couldn’t even see their home from this far.

It was hard to accept they had traveled so far so quickly, but it was the truth. Her Leon might be even stronger than she had thought—traversing five whole kilometers in a couple of seconds? That just sounded unreal.
"Hang on tight. The ride ahead might be a bit bumpy," his calm voice sounded in her ear.
She naturally tightened her grip on him, but she was still trying to process the feat her disciple had just performed.
Leon was already using the wind element to cancel out the pressure she would feel when traveling at such speed. He could easily make her avoid feeling any bumps.

But how could he miss such an opportunity to see his master’s bountiful breasts jiggle naturally? Even though he saw them regularly and felt them thoroughly, this was a different feeling he couldn’t miss out on.
His spatial awareness—50 meters around him—was enough to see every movement, even with his eyes closed, so his focus was only on her chest.

Once again, he began traveling at his ultra-fast speed. Because of the terrain—its ups and downs—he had to make small jumps from time to time. He couldn’t help but make Seraphine feel the bumps, as his eyes were glued to the jiggle of her softness.

After two minutes of lightning-fast travel, Leon finally had to stop. The Rocky Mountain plain was much bigger than he had anticipated. He had traversed around 250 kilometers in a single direction to reach the end.
Seraphine, who had tried to look at the world around her while he was traveling—but failed to see a thing because of the speed—finally looked ahead when they stopped.

From high up, hundreds of meters above, she could see in front of her an ever-stretching grassland. As far as she could see, there was only grass—no trees, no animals, no rocks, no mountains, or anything else.
Just endless green.
Even with its weirdness, as in the real world, seeing something like this would have been impossible—it still looked beautiful.
"Leon, isn’t it beautiful?"
"Yes, very beautiful, Seraphine."
Despite looking unnaturally alone, they agreed it was indeed a beautiful sight, especially from so high up.
He couldn’t help but bring his lips closer to hers and give her a long, romantic kiss while she was still in his arms.
Seraphine loved it. After the kiss, they stayed still for a while, enjoying the beauty of this unnatural sight.
She noticed the rough pathway leading downward. She knew it wouldn’t even be a challenge for him, and she pointed it out to Leon.
"Leon, look, we can go down from there."
He didn’t even glance in that direction, as he had already seen the pathway.
But he didn’t need it—when such a beautiful way to go down was already in front of him, why bother with that rocky terrain?
He jumped down without any warning.

Seraphine panicked at his sudden jump. Her eyes shook in shock—they were more than 1,000 meters above the ground, a height she couldn’t even compare to the mountains he had destroyed and boasted about.
As the biggest one he had told her about was only 800 meters tall.
"Calm down, Seraphine. Just look around. Isn’t it beautiful?"
His soothing voice made her heart settle.

The first thing she looked at was him—his long silver-white hair flowed with the wind, the softness in his gaze as he looked at her with those mystical eyes, his sharp features, small nose, inviting lips, and extremely handsome face.
She couldn’t help but be in a daze for a second.
It really is as beautiful as you say, my Love, perhaps even more so than you realized. I can live my whole life just looking at this sight.
